articles.title: Grading MLB's Biggest Offseason Deals, Including Maikel Garcia To Mariners
articles.summary: We're grading MLB's most notable free agent deals and how they impact the teams involved.
articles.body: Baseball’s hot stove is warming up as teams look to upgrade their rosters before the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement on Dec. 1. We're waiting to see where this offseason's top free agents, like two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal or star Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato will land. As more players come off the board, we're grading notable deals and how they impact the teams involved. JUMP TO: White Sox Ship Castillo | Garcia To Seattle | Twins Sign Gray | White Sox Sign May | Red Sox Sign Bauers | Braves Sign Phillips RHPs Castillo, Martin Traded To Rockies Colorado receives: RHP Luis Castillo and RHP Davis Martin Chicago receives: LHP Sean Sullivan and minor-league C Douglas Veliz Grade for Rockies: B- Grade for White Sox: Incomplete Breaking Down The Deal: This one came as a surprise, considering the White Sox just added Dustin May to try to bolster a rotation that was a weak spot last season. Now they’re taking two starting pitching options away. It’s an acknowledgment of the mistake they made when they traded for Castillo at last season’s deadline, a move that seemed risky for a White Sox team that needed more reliability from its starting pitchers. At the time, Castillo had a 5.06 ERA, the lowest strikeout rate of his career, concerning underlying numbers and a contract few would have been willing to take on. The White Sox did it anyway, getting some salary relief by sending reliever Seranthony Dominguez back to Seattle along with a legitimate prospect in Boston Smith. It all ended badly, as many feared, with Castillo registering an 8.42 ERA over nine appearances in Chicago and losing his spot in the White Sox rotation. Now, to move Castillo’s $22.75 million salary, they had to include a valuable big-league starter in Martin. Getting off the Castillo contract probably deserves a C here, but for now it gets an incomplete because this grade is entirely dependent on what the White Sox do with those savings. Neither Sullivan, a left-handed pitcher who debuted last year for the Rockies, nor Veliz, a 17-year-old catcher out of Venezuela who’s more of a dart throw, are particularly highly-regarded prospects. The White Sox now must meaningfully upgrade the rotation with pieces better than Castillo and Martin. The Rockies were going to have their hands full convincing starting pitchers to go to Colorado on the open market, so it’s possible the additions of Castillo and Martin were better than anything they could have done in free agency. Castillo is coming off the worst season of his career and just allowed the highest pulled fly ball rate of his career — not a great sign as he heads to Coors Field! — but he is a three-time All-Star who had produced an ERA under 4.00 in seven straight seasons before his 2026 implosion. The bigger get is Martin, who had an All-Star caliber first half for the White Sox (9-4, 3.41 ERA) before free-falling in the second half (0-4, 5.12). Martin’s 45.1% hard-hit rate last year could spell trouble in Colorado, but he finished the year with a 3.95 ERA and he represents an upgrade for a Rockies pitching staff that needs all the help it can get. - Kavner ↑ Return To Top Of Article Mariners Get 3B Garcia In 6-Player Deal Seattle receives: 3B Maikel Garcia, RHP James McArthur and a minor league reliever Kansas City receives: RHP Bryce Miller, LHP Jose Ferrer and RHP Logan Evans Grade for Mariners: A- Grade for Royals: C Breaking Down The Deal: For years, we have been waiting for the Mariners to trade away someone, anyone, from their gigantic reserve of pitchers to help address some of their immediate needs. Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto made it clear at November's GM Meetings that the club’s biggest priority this offseason was to improve their defense, particularly on the left field of the infield. Garcia is one of the best defensive third basemen in the league. He had a down year offensively this past season, when he was limited to just 82 games after dealing with multiple injuries. Garcia is still just 26 years old, and in a healthy year, he should be expected to replicate his 2025 All-Star season, when he hit .286/.351/.449 (121 OPS+). So, for Seattle, this trade makes sense in its efforts to win now and repeat the deep postseason run it enjoyed in 2025. The Mariners have needed an everyday bat for a while now, and their surplus of arms made this deal possible. Garcia headlines a three-player package that also includes a pair of relievers, with McArthur having some closing experience with subpar results. Even despite losing Miller to the Royals in this trade, the Mariners still have a solid rotation led by Logan Gilbert, Bryan Woo and George Kirby. Losing Ferrer hurts Seattle, but Dipoto should be able to beef up his bullpen in other ways this winter. As for the Royals’ end of this, I have some questions. Who’s going to play third base with Garcia out of the picture? And why trade the young franchise cornerstone Kansas City just signed to a five-year extension less than a year ago? If the bottom line for the Royals is that they needed pitching help, there are multiple mid-rotation starters available in free agency this offseason, and they wouldn’t even need to break the bank to shore up the rotation while also keeping Garcia. Take, for instance, free-agent right-hander Michael Soroka. The Athletic projected Soroka to land a three-year contract in the range of $54 million. Soroka is even coming off a better season than Miller, who dealt with elbow-related injuries in 2026, which led to a dip in performance and even a demotion to the bullpen in the second half of the season. Even though Kansas City did well to acquire three pitchers in one trade, it seems like the Royals could’ve addressed their lack of arms by spending some money, without trading away their third baseman of the future. — Thosar ↑ Return To Top Of Article Twins Sign RHP Sonny Gray Contract: Two years, $55 million (including an opt-out) Grade: B+ Breaking Down The Deal: One way to help a bullpen in need? Get a standout starter who doesn’t need much assistance in the middle innings. Gray is coming off a stellar season in Boston in which he went 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA and finished fifth in American League Cy Young voting. And, as he will tell you, he was particularly good the longer a game went on. "I think I’m the best pitcher in the American League going through the order the third time," Gray said while frustrated after getting pulled with two outs in the fifth inning of Boston’s Game 2 wild-card loss to the Yankees. "I think that’s a fact." Indeed, Gray was exceptional last season against opponents the third time through the order, holding them to a .180/.235/.280 slash line in those situations. That ability should be especially helpful to the Twins, who have yet to address a bullpen that ranked in the bottom five in MLB in ERA and WHIP. While there is risk in giving multiple years to a 37-year-old — especially one whose strikeout rate has dipped from 30.3% in 2024 to 26.7% in 2025 and 21.8% in 2026 — this signing could help turn the Twins’ rotation into a real strength if Pablo López returns from Tommy John surgery looking like himself again. It’s also a positive sign that the Twins, after years of cutting payroll, will take necessary steps to try to contend in a winnable division. Gray, who was an All-Star with the Twins in 2023, has already demonstrated his ability to succeed in Minnesota, and his extensive pitch mix could allow him to continue succeeding deep into his 30s despite the red flags with his whiff rate. He has also been a model of reliability, having thrown more than 160 innings each of the past four seasons. The Twins still need to add relief help, but bringing back catcher Ryan Jeffers and adding Gray is a strong start to free agency. - Kavner ↑ Return To Top Of Article White Sox Sign RHP Dustin May Contract: Three years, $52.5 million Grade: C+ Breaking Down This Deal: The White Sox needed to stabilize their rotation this winter after getting the fewest innings from their starting pitchers of any team in MLB. May provides depth to the group as a high-upside mid-rotation arm, though his injury history and inconsistencies on the mound present risk for a team that needs innings and reliability. May’s 145 innings last season between the Cardinals and Brewers represented a career high. He demonstrated his high ceiling with a complete-game shutout against the Padres on June 15, and the eventual World Series champions thought highly enough of May’s tools to make him their main pitching addition at the deadline after he posted a 4.38 ERA in 22 starts in St. Louis. But his numbers dipped in the second half in Milwaukee. May had a 5.65 ERA in 10 regular-season starts with the Brewers and a 5.73 ERA in five playoff appearances. His fastball velocity (96.9 mph), good extension off the mound using his 6-foot-6-inch frame and better-than-average strikeout rate, walk rate and overall stuff give reason to believe the 29-year-old’s best could still be ahead. But this was a rather significant commitment given his actual performance to this point, and I expected the White Sox to be shopping a tier above on the starting pitching market to address their biggest need. Perhaps that still happens. - Kavner ↑ Return To Top Of Article Red Sox Sign 1B Jake Bauers Contract: Four years, $58 million Grade: B Breaking Down This Deal: Never give up, kids. A couple years ago, Bauers was considering retirement. Now look at him. Of the eight players given the one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, Bauers seemed perhaps the likeliest candidate to accept. After all, if he produced at the same level again next season, that would make more teams willing to believe his breakout and allow him to cash in again in 2028. Instead, the Red Sox were willing to pounce in their search for power, and the 31-year-old slugger opted for the long-term security of a four-year deal. Boston is banking on Bauers building off his career year in Milwaukee, a season in which he ranked seventh in MLB in wRC+ and tied for 10th in OPS and came up clutch in October. There is obvious risk involved. Entering 2026, the journeyman had a career .672 OPS and had never hit more than 12 home runs in a season. Bauers will cost the Red Sox their second and fifth-highest draft selections, and the fit is imperfect. Boston’s best hitter this year was its first baseman, Willson Contreras. Those two now figure to split first base and DH duties, leaving even fewer at-bats available for the surplus of Red Sox outfielders, which might necessitate a trade. But the Red Sox, who finished 26th in home runs and 21st in walks, saw an opportunity to acquire a talent who could help in both areas. The underlying numbers suggest Bauers’ breakout was real, and if he plays the way he did last year for the next four seasons, his $14.5 million average annual salary will look like a steal. — Kavner ↑ Return To Top Of Article Braves Sign RHP Evan Phillips Contract: Three years, $35 million Grade: B- Breaking Down This Deal: While the team’s more glaring need is starting pitching, the Braves had some work to do if they wanted to maintain one of the best bullpens in the sport with closer Raisel Iglesias reaching free agency. The addition of Phillips, who was one of MLB’s best relievers when healthy over the last six years with the Dodgers, should help. Signing him now also provides the Braves some flexibility as the offseason continues. They could still sign another closer and have Phillips, Robert Suarez or Dylan Lee pitching high-leverage innings, or they could roll with any of those three for the ninth inning while turning their attention to their more glaring needs (starting pitching, shortstop). It also gives them more freedom to decide the role they want for versatile 21-year-old Didier Fuentes. For Phillips, the deal marks a return to where it all began. The 32-year-old was drafted by the Braves in 2015 and debuted with the team in 2018 before being traded to Baltimore. He was released in 2021, signed a minor-league deal with the Rays, got designated for assignment and was claimed by the Dodgers, where he turned his career around, producing a 2.36 ERA with 254 strikeouts and 46 saves in 221 innings over the last six seasons. Phillips returned from Tommy John surgery last season and averaged the highest four-seam velocity of his career. He was also barreled more than ever before — which, in tandem with the highest fly-ball rate and lowest ground-ball rate of his career, led to him surrendering five home runs in 26 innings — but he struck out 33 batters with just six walks, and his stuff looked better as the year progressed. Over the last two months of the season, Phillips had a 2.41 ERA with 24 strikeouts and four walks in 18.2 innings. He then made five scoreless appearances in the postseason. It’s an expensive price for a reliever who might not be their closer and a pitcher who has thrown just 86.1 regular-season innings over the last three seasons. But as long as he is healthy, the addition of Phillips should keep Atlanta’s bullpen a strength. — Kavner ↑ Return To Top Of Article MLB Related StoriesThe Top 50 MLB Free Agents Of The 2026-27 Offseason, RankedBiggest Offseason Needs For All 30 MLB TeamsPredictions On Who Will Sign MLB's Top Free Agents, Including Tarik Skubal

articles.title: Week 12 College Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Playoff lineup advice from Eric Froton
articles.summary: Eric Froton gets you ready for the college fantasy football playoffs with start/sit advice for key players at each position.
articles.body:
College fantasy football playoffs are here, and with them come a series of tough lineup decisions that can make or break your season. Every lineup choice is under a microscope, so here are my start-sit calls for Week 12. Good luck!

Arizona's all-time leading passer, Fifita is completing 71.7% of his passes at 9.0 yards per attempt. He's having his finest season from a fantasy perspective, averaging 25.4 PPG and ranking ninth in total points scored at the position. The fifth-year signal-caller has thrown for 280+ yards in eight straight appearances while cashing in 2+ touchdowns in seven of those contests. His opponent this week, Kansas State, is 1-6 versus Power Four teams and has been relentlessly attacked vertically, averaging 9.2 air yards per target (128th) with 18.5% of completions gaining 20+ yards (110th). With Arizona ranking 12th nationally in SP+ offense averaging 6.5 yards per play, Fifita should once again clear the 25-point mark and is well worth starting in the first week of the playoffs.

Iowa State has looked reborn, averaging 41 points over the last three games, with Raynor scoring 29+ points in two of those contests. His balanced rushing/passing profile offers a stable floor against UCF's leaky secondary that ranks 109th in explosive pass rate and allows 6.8 yards per dropback (108th).

Kansas is 2-6 against P4 opponents and allows explosive pass plays 18.5% of the time (110th). Bachmeier has scored 27+ points in four of his last six appearances and should have little trouble dicing up the Jayhawks' secondary that ranks 126th in havoc rate.

Dierre Hill Jr., Oregon at Michigan State

Hill has taken over the primary rushing duties since Jordon Davison went down with a lower-leg injury that will cause him to miss a third straight game. Despite facing two excellent defenses in Ohio State and Michigan over the last two weeks, Hill thrived, scoring 24.6 and 21.2 points as the increased workload (39 touches in total) directly translated into fantasy production. Since replacement QB Dylan Raiola has settled into the starting role, the Ducks have rattled off three straight victories and face a Michigan State defense which ranks 102nd in rushing success rate (44.6%) and 94th allowing 33.4 yards per drive. Hill's roster rate has shot up to 86% and he's a locked-in starter for as long as Davison is out of action for the resurgent Ducks.

Cardae Mack, Arizona State vs. Oklahoma State

The Mack Daddy generated substantial preseason buzz in a competitive ASU running back room, which hinted at the true freshman taking over the starting job from Kyson Brown at some point in the season.

Mack didn't officially wrest control of the backfield until Week 8, when he ripped Kansas State for 26 carries, 159 yards and four touchdowns for a career-high 41.1 points. He has recorded 15+ points in five of his last six games and has received 27 red-zone carries, which he converted into six touchdowns. Mack (5'10"/215 lbs) runs with a punishing style and refuses to avoid contact, instead preferring to lower the boom and pancake would-be tacklers.

The Sun Devils play an Oklahoma State defense that allowed 50+ points to both Iowa State and Texas Tech over the last three weeks, and allows 5.8 yards per play (98th) with 7.6% of plays generating 20+ yards (121st). I expect ASU to ply Mack with 26+ touches for the fifth straight game, which should result in another 20+ point performance this Saturday.

A true heavy-usage workhorse, Ford is averaging 31.5 PPG with 24+ touches in each of his last four games. He should once again erupt for 20+ points against a reeling Cal defense that ranks 121st in yards per carry.

One of the most intriguing late-season risers at the RB position, Young is coming off two games with 20+ points in his last three appearances, and faces an absolutely pitiful Cincinnati defense that just allowed 46.9 fantasy points to ISU star Aiden Flora. He's a strong flex play versus the Bearcats' struggling defensive front that ranks 123rd in rushing success rate.

Arguably the most explosive receiver in the country, Malachi Toney caught an astounding 86% of his 85 targets before sustaining an ankle injury that will sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. His absence opens the door for Duke transfer Barkate to take over as the primary aerial weapon, and he has excelled, catching 84% of his targets while putting up 22 points against the elite Notre Dame secondary and securing eight receptions for a season-high 134 yards last week versus his former team, Duke. He should be a fixture in CFF lineups against a Virginia Tech defense that ranks 113th nationally in wide open target rate (28%) and 106th in adjusted net yards per pass attempt (9.0).

Mosley joins the likes of freshman phenom WRs Jesse Legree and Legend Glasker in having captured the admiration of the CFB-watching public with their highlight-reel-worthy receiving acumen. He started his collegiate career with two 100-yard performances before suffering an injury in Week 3 that kept him out for a month. Since returning, Mosley has recorded 17+ points and 100+ yards in four of his last five contests, including a nine-reception, 130-yard showing against Indiana's second-ranked defense. USC lines up against a Maryland program in transition after firing HC Mike Locksley, ranking 106th in points per drive with a 71% adjusted completion rate allowed. Mosley is a top-10 starting option this week and is a must-start versus a floundering Terps' secondary.

Tre Richardson, Louisville vs. Pittsburgh

Pitt has one of the most bankable imbalanced defenses in the P4, ranking first nationally allowing 3.3 yards per carry, but ranking 127th allowing wide open targets on 31% of throws while allowing 16.3 yards per successful dropback (123rd). Richardson is a speed demon who should catch a long touchdown from QB Lincoln Kienholz.

Sowell has quietly been the engine of Penn State's pass game after WR Koby Howard went down with a season-ending injury. He should score 15+ points for the fourth time in the last six games against a Rutgers defense that is one of the three worst defenses in all of P4 football.

The Ohio State transfer has been as consistently productive as any tight end in the country, putting up 10+ points and 50+ yards in six of his last seven contests. Thurman has established himself as UNC's unquestioned red-zone maven, receiving 18 targets, catching 10 for a whopping seven red-zone scores. He has caught at least five passes in six of his last seven games, and should have success once again versus a UVA defense that ranks 98th in explosive completion rate and 121st with 55% of completions gaining first-down yardage. Arguably the most projectable and safest player among all P4 tight ends, Thurman should be active and in your lineup.

Similar to his teammate Barkate, Lofton has seen an uptick in targets and production since Toney went down. He has an enticing matchup against a Virginia Tech defense that just allowed Stanford TE Benji Blackburn to lead the Cardinal in receiving with 63 yards in a 40-22 blowout of the Hokies last week.

SMU is in the midst of its toughest two-game stretch of the season, and failed the first test in spectacular fashion by getting eviscerated 49-7 by Wake Forest last weekend. Jennings was totally flummoxed by the Demon Deacons' secondary, producing just 10.9 points and continuing a troubling trend where he has scored 24+ points just once in his last seven games against P4 foes. His lack of rushing potency has really suppressed Jennings' fantasy upside, and he now has to face Notre Dame's top flight secondary that ranks seventh in yards per dropback (4.9) and ninth in explosive completion rate allowed. I simply cannot trust the immobile pocket distributor on the road against a legitimate national title contender in Notre Dame.

Leavitt had a good run against the lower echelon defenses of the SEC, but he has been bottled up by Alabama and Texas, scoring 15.8 and 14.5 points in the last two weeks. He now has to face a Tennessee secondary that ranks third in air yards per target (5.4) and yards per dropback allowed (4.6), while pitching three-and-outs 44.6% of the time (1st in FBS). Don't risk your playoff life on Leavitt's interception-prone arm.

Raymond was one of my most prominent "fades" of the preseason after he was so volume reliant in order to be productive last year, leaning on his 244 carries to fuel his 20.5 PPG average. However, Rutgers' dismal 125th-ranked defense is statistically the second-worst defense among all P4 programs and puts the RU offense at a major disadvantage, leading to extremely pass-tilted game scripts. For his part, Raymond has eclipsed the 13-point barrier just one time in his last six appearances, with a combined 10.3 points generated over the last two games in which Rutgers scored just 10 total points. He faces a Penn State defense that ranks 10th in three-and-out rate (39%) and 23rd in rushing success rate allowed (37%), with all the factors mentioned leaving me to believe Raymond will once again disappoint fantasy managers who rely on him to bring home a playoff-winning performance this weekend.

The Mustangs were thoroughly dominated by Wake Forest by a score of 49-7, with Raphael converting 15 carries into a mere 54 yards. Raphael's ceiling for this game is 12 points, meaning you cannot rely on him in a playoff scenario.

An undersized rusher who is known for his big-play ability, Brown has not received the volume the CFF community expected after managing just 36 yards on 16 carries versus Ole Miss in Week 1. He has scored under 14 points in three of his last four, and plays a Pitt defense that will let you throw all day on them, as discussed earlier, but smothers the run game allowing a mere 0.8 yards before contact (1st in FBS).

Roebuck was the preseason favorite to replace departed Washington WR1 Denzel Boston, with Rashid Williams also receiving favorable press for his play in fall camp. I had the opportunity to watch Roebuck play against UCLA last year, when he popped catching 7-of-10 passes for 96 yards and a touchdown. He has been pounded with 90 targets this season and had a nice midseason run where he scored 15+ points in four-of-five games. However, over his last three appearances that production has fallen off, with Roebuck producing just 81 receiving yards and a touchdown in that timeframe.

It appears that he has fallen behind WR Chris Lawson in the pecking order, as Lawson has scored in double digits in each of his last six games, with 20+ points in three of those contests. Compounding matters is a ferocious Indiana defense that ranks second nationally and allows just 1.1 points per drive (4th), and Roebuck sporting an ankle injury that will assuredly slow him down if he's able to suit up. With a diminishing role and an injury slowing him down, I'm benching Roebuck in favor of Lawson.

Oregon WR Jeremiah McClellan got hurt early in the year after erupting for 150 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 versus Boise State, looking like he was ready to emerge as the Ducks' WR2 alongside Dak Moore. Stewart was very productive early in the season, but has failed to score 10+ points since Week 6 versus UCLA. I fear Stewart is now the fourth option with McClellan's return, meaning you cannot put him in your lineup.

Trying to figure out which games Faison will be fantasy relevant has been a weekly game of Whack-A-Mole. He has failed to hit the 10-point mark in five of his last eight appearances, and Notre Dame could simply decide to bulldoze the inferior SMU defensive line, which clouds Faison's profile this week. I am staying away this week.

Pittman has been splitting work with TE Theo Ohrstrom, and just popped off for five receptions for 76 yards in a pass-heavy situation, where SMU was defeated 49-7 by Wake Forest. Prior to Saturday, Pittman had scored just 9.5 total points over the previous three games, and now has to play Notre Dame's top flight secondary that ranks seventh nationally in yards per dropback allowed (4.9). With Ohrstrom providing internal competition catching 18 passes for 217 yards and four touchdowns, in addition to facing Notre Dame's smothering secondary, I am sitting Pittman this week and think he regresses after a rare boom week versus the Demon Deacons.

The Bears have fired their HC Dave Aranda, and just got embarrassed by BYU, averaging just 4.3 yards per attempt for 238 total yards versus the Cougars. For his part, Livingston took a step back by failing to secure either of his targets. The Red Raiders rank second in FBS with an 8.6% linebacker havoc rate, and 14th in suppressing explosive pass plays. Livingston is a product of his offense, which may or may not be able to move the ball on Tech. Don't take the chance, leave Livingston on the bench.

articles.body: Vuelve LaL iga con nuevo líder en la Top Movistar de los premiazos. Tras sumar 203 puntos en las dos últimas jornadas, José María Moreno Martín (Madrid, 46 años) se puso al frente del concurso con más de 2.500 euros en recompensas. Es biólogo, aficionado del Madrid y rompería la hucha por Bellingham. “Al Fantasy hay que dedicarle 20 minutos todas las mañanas para gestionar fichajes y ventas. Hacer un equipo pensando en el corto, medio y largo plazo. “Mientras espero los trenes de Cercanías de Madrid tengo mucho tiempo para revisar los equipos". José María juega doce ligas oficiales del Movistar Fantasy MARCA. También lidera la del tiktoker Deivysun, va segundo en la Tertulia Sports y en El Azteca y cada jornada tiene que decidir once capitanes (en todas menos la Top MARCA): “Da aliciente al juego y permite que se puedan recuperar grandes desventajas arriesgando.” José María, que trabaja como Facultativo Especialista de Bioquímica Clínica, está sorprendido por el gran rendimiento de Güler y "decepcionado con el de Sancet, que ha sido mi peor fichaje. El mejor fue el de Raphinha". Disfruta mucho con el Movistar Fantasy MARCA porque es un juego "divertido y no requiere de mucho tiempo. Le da una emoción especial a cada jornada y permite picarte en el buen sentido con amigos, demostrar conocimientos de fútbol y estrategia. Y da la posibilidad de ganar premios”. El rey de la liga con mejores regalos nos deja su equipazo para la Jornada Movistar. ¡Gracias crack y mucha suerte! ¡Descarga aquí el Movistar Fantasy MARCA con más novedades que nunca! Con todas las competiciones: Champions, Segunda, Liga F, Premier, Serie A, Ligue 1... ¡Más premios! ¡Y con más opciones de personalización! Síguenos en X @FantasyMARCA. articles.title: Cuatro surfistas, dos títulos y una última batalla en Laredo
articles.standfirst: La playa cántabra de La Salvé decide la Liga EDP Surf Pro Spain 2026 con Adriana Hidalgo y Alfonso Suárez al frente de la clasificación, aunque sus perseguidores todavía pueden arrebatarles la corona.
articles.summary: La playa cántabra de La Salvé decide la Liga EDP Surf Pro Spain 2026 con Adriana Hidalgo y Alfonso Suárez al frente de la clasificación, aunque sus perseguidores todavía pueden arrebatarles la corona.
articles.body: El surf español afronta su último gran duelo de la temporada en las aguas del Cantábrico. La playa de La Salvé, en Laredo, acoge desde este viernes 20 de noviembre la tercera y definitiva prueba de la Liga EDP Surf Pro Spain 2026, con los títulos masculino y femenino todavía por decidir. Adriana Hidalgo (1.860 puntos) y Alfonso Suárez (1.670) llegan como líderes, pero el particular sistema de puntuación del circuito abre la puerta a una resolución inesperada: Nora Álvarez y Sean Gunning, ambos novenos o más atrás en sus respectivas clasificaciones, pueden proclamarse campeones si vuelven a ganar. La clave está en el reglamento. Aunque el circuito consta de tres pruebas —Somo, Gijón y Laredo—, solo cuentan los dos mejores resultados de cada participante. Cada victoria otorga 1.000 puntos y, en caso de empate, entra en juego la puntuación descartada. En categoría femenina, Adriana Hidalgo llega con ventaja después de ganar en Somo y terminar segunda en Gijón. La siguen Sol Borelli (1.400 puntos) y Sara Romeo (1.230). Sin embargo, la principal amenaza podría llegar desde la sexta posición: Nora Álvarez, vencedora en Gijón, alcanzaría los 2.000 puntos si repite triunfo en Laredo, una cifra que le garantizaría el campeonato. En el cuadro masculino, Alfonso Suárez encabeza la general por delante de Alejandro Sancho (1.470) y Bitor Garitaonandia (1.460). Los tres mantienen opciones, pero el escenario más llamativo lo protagoniza Sean Gunning. El ganador de Gijón ocupa actualmente la novena posición y, pese a ello, también sería campeón si conquista La Invernal. La undécima edición de La Invernal de Laredo se disputa en uno de los arenales más emblemáticos del norte de España. Con más de cuatro kilómetros de longitud y olas que rompen tanto a derechas como a izquierdas, La Salvé ofrece un escenario exigente en el que la elección de cada ola puede marcar diferencias. La organización había establecido un periodo de espera hasta el 20 de diciembre para aprovechar las mejores condiciones posibles, pero las previsiones favorables han permitido activar la competición este viernes. La prueba, organizada por la Escuela Surf Pinos junto a La Invernal, es gratuita para los espectadores y forma parte de un circuito que reparte 33.000 euros en premios durante toda la temporada. Tras las victorias de Hidalgo y Suárez en Somo y de Álvarez y Gunning en Gijón, Laredo pondrá el cierre a una temporada especialmente abierta. Los líderes tienen el título al alcance de la mano, pero sus perseguidores todavía pueden cambiarlo todo. En La Salvé no bastará con defender la ventaja: habrá que salir a buscar las olas que deciden un campeonato.

articles.title: NHL trade rumor: What does Pat Brisson's latest response reveal about Sidney Crosby's future with the struggling Pittsburgh Penguins
articles.summary: Explore the latest news on Sidney Crosby's uncertain future with the Pittsburgh Penguins as agent Pat Brisson provides insights amid the team's disappointing season. Discover potential trade rumors and organizational strategies.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Penguins are headed toward more uncertainty on their long-term direction, with captain Sidney Crosby’s future becoming an increasingly important part of the conversation. Agent Pat Brisson recently addressed the situation after general manager Kyle Dubas indicated that Crosby would have a say in determining his future with the organization.Pittsburgh's disappointing 7-11-2 start has placed the franchise among the NHL's struggling teams. As the potential for forward-looking roster moves comes into focus, Crosby's contract has been of interest around the league.Why Sidney Crosby's future with Pittsburgh Penguins remains uncertainSidney Crosby's future with the Pittsburgh Penguins remains uncertain because the team's poor results, upcoming contract decision and general manager Kyle Dubas' long-term strategy could influence what happens next.Crosby's agent, Pat Brisson, offered a measured response on Thursday, November 19, after Dubas discussed the captain's future during his media availability a day earlier.According to NHL insider Pierre LeBrun, Brisson said: "Sidney has been in Pittsburgh for over 20 years and he isn't in any rush to make a decision. Kyle will do what he feels is best for the organization in the meantime."The statement doesn't indicate Crosby wants to leave Pittsburgh or that a trade is an imminent possibility. Instead, it indicates that the veteran forward is taking his time while allowing the organization to determine its next steps.Kyle Dubas signals future-focused Penguins roster changesDubas spoke about the Penguins’ disappointing season during a Nov. 18 media availability. The general manager acknowledged the team's inconsistency and suggested that the organization would prioritize its long-term competitiveness if results did not improve.The Penguins joined the conversation with a 7-11-2 record in 20 games, 15th in the Eastern Conference and 28th in the overall NHL standings.Dubas said future moves will be more about adding younger pieces that can help the franchise in its next competitive window rather than short-term additions.Why Sidney Crosby's contract situation mattersCrosby is playing the final season of his two-year contract and is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent on July 1, 2027.The 39-year-old captain has spent his entire NHL career with Pittsburgh, winning three Stanley Cup championships in 2009, 2016 and 2017. Any potential departure is a big deal for the organization and its fans, given his history with the franchise.According to Daily Faceoff, Crosby has tallied six goals and seven assists for 13 points through 20 games in 2026-27.A decision about his future could depend on Pittsburgh's performance, the team's rebuilding direction and his own desire to continue competing with the franchise.Could an NHL blockbuster trade become possible?A potential Sidney Crosby trade remains a possibility rather than a confirmed development. The Colorado Avalanche and Montreal Canadiens have been mentioned in trade speculation, but there is no known agreement or official indication that either team is working on a deal.For now, the Penguins' immediate priority is improving their performances and assessing their position as the season progresses.Brisson’s answer keeps the door open, but Dubas has made it crystal clear that the long-term interests of the organization will dictate future decisions. Pittsburgh's results over the coming weeks could therefore play an important role in determining whether Crosby continues his career with the Penguins beyond this season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Gavin McKenna faces NHL scrutiny after controversial moment against Los Angeles Kings sparks backlash among Toronto Maple Leafs fans
articles.summary: Toronto Maple Leafs forward Gavin McKenna faces criticism after pulling away from a puck battle in a crucial game against the Los Angeles Kings, leading to a frustrating 4-3 loss for the team.
articles.body: Gavin McKenna is facing criticism from Toronto Maple Leafs fans after a broadcast moment during Thursday's NHL matchup against the Los Angeles Kings attracted attention online. The young forward appeared to pull away from a puck battle involving Kings forward Samuel Helenius rather than continue the contest near the boards.The incident became another talking point after Toronto surrendered a three-goal advantage and eventually lost 4-3 in a shootout at Scotiabank Arena. McKenna was not solely to blame for the Maple Leafs’ implosion, but his decision in the second period didn’t help the frustration surrounding the team’s play.Gavin McKenna faces criticism against the Los Angeles KingsGavin McKenna's decision to pull away from a puck battle against Samuel Helenius became a major talking point among Toronto Maple Leafs supporters during the November 19 matchup.During the game, McKenna was involved in a sequence along the boards when Samuel Helenius challenged him for possession. As the physical contest developed, the Toronto forward appeared to retreat rather than continue battling for the puck.The play got attention because it showed McKenna backpedaling from the developing play, thereby allowing the Los Angeles Kings to gain possession. The moment was particularly noticeable during a game in which Toronto was attempting to maintain control after establishing an early advantage.The reaction was to the apparent lack of commitment on the puck battle. A few unhappy fans questioned why McKenna didn’t try to keep the ball on the ground more, while a few more saw the sequence as a taste of the kind of fire expected from players wearing Toronto.The criticism also came at an inopportune moment for the franchise. The Maple Leafs entered the matchup looking to improve their results, making every individual mistake and questionable decision more noticeable.How did the Los Angeles Kings complete their comeback?Toronto initially appeared to have control of the contest. Auston Matthews opened the scoring with a power-play goal before John Tavares extended the advantage. Dakota Joshua then made it 3-0 early in the second period.However, the Los Angeles Kings responded with three goals in less than 12 minutes.Alex Turcotte started the comeback at 2:55 of the second period, followed by Alex Laferriere's power-play goal at 10:11. Erik Haula completed the comeback by tying the score at 3-3 at 14:51.Neither team managed to find a winner during the third period or overtime. Adrian Kempe eventually scored the decisive shootout goal, giving Los Angeles a 4-3 victory.According to the NHL's official game recap, the defeat extended Toronto's winless run to eight games, with the Maple Leafs recording a 0-7-1 stretch during that period.The viral sequence is yet another layer of difficulty for McKenna as the team looks for consistency. The attention surrounding his effort also reflects the growing expectations placed on young players in Toronto.The Maple Leafs are concentrating on fixing their team’s problems, not allowing one controversial moment to distract from the bigger issues that led to their latest loss.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Week 11 Fantasy Football Fades and Busts: Sorry, but Jalen Coker SZN looks like it's over
articles.summary: Matt Okada takes you through 6 players he's avoiding in fantasy football for Week 11.
articles.body:
Welcome to the 11th of 17 weekly articles spotlighting the fantasy football fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until the fantasy championships.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 11 of the 2026 season.

QB Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears

It's the Bye-pocalypse and you're looking for streamers with Jordan Love or Matthew Stafford on bye (or Drake Maye hurt). I get it. But Tyler Shough is not the answer this week. After his strong three-game start to the season, Shough has thrown multiple touchdown passes just once in six games since and scored fewer than 16 fantasy points in four of those six games. Over that span, his 5.9 yards per attempt are the fourth-lowest among qualified QBs, capped by the fifth-lowest explosive pass rate (10.0%).

And while the Bears might look like a decent matchup in your fantasy app, things have changed with the arrival of Jeffery Simmons. Through the first seven weeks, they had allowed a 102.8 passer rating (sixth-highest) and 18.8% explosive pass rate (third-highest), with the NFL's highest yards per attempt (8.7). In the two games with Simmons, they've dropped to a 64.6 passer rating, 13.3% explosive pass rate and just 6.5 yards per attempt. And while they do force higher volume by merit of their productive offense, Shough's inefficiency the last two months cancels out a lot of that volume. He has a low floor and a low ceiling in a game that could go sideways quickly.

If at all possible, stream someone with more security, more upside or both.

What to do ❓ Shough is outside QB1 range and should even be benched for typically iffy streamers like Bo Nix, Kirk Cousins, Cam Ward and possibly even Bryce Young.

RB Travis Etienne Jr., New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears

Can you tell how badly I fear this upgraded Bears defense? Travis Etienne Jr. is the official name here, as he is the highest ranked and projected of the Saints running back trio, but to be clear, we're fading the entire backfield. In a heavily mix-and-match season, no New Orleans back has logged more than 10 carries in multiple games. And it's only gotten worse now that Etienne, Alvin Kamara and Audric Estimé are all healthy, active and involved at the same time . Last week against the Panthers — in what should have been an excellent matchup — they split the snaps 44% (Estimé) to 34% (Etienne) to 23% (Kamara). Etienne "led" the trio with eight carries, but Estimé had seven and neither back topped 40 total yards. And then, of course, Kamara vultured both touchdowns on just five total touches.

Etienne should jump Estimé in snap share in his second game back, but all the evidence suggests that both Estimé and Kamara will continue stealing valuable touches and scoring opportunities. Take the entire messy package and pit it against Simmons and the rest of the Bears defense and you get an easy triple-fade. None of this trio are Bucky Irving (who had a great day against Chicago). In fact, they're a far more fitting comparison for the Seahawks committee, which totaled 10 fantasy points against the Bears in Week 8.

Etienne would need a lucky touchdown to hit double-digit fantasy points and both of the others could score and still fall short this weekend.

What to do ❓ Bench Etienne outside of the most desperate of situations, and sit Estimé and Kamara even in those situations. None of them are close to RB2 range and even Etienne is towards the back of RB3 territory this week.

Those of us who rode with Braelon Allen as a strong RB2 through Breece Hall's extended absence might have a tough time sending him back to the bench. It's time. He has totaled just 9.5 fantasy points in the two games since Hall returned, on 19 total opportunities, and is clearly the secondary option in general and a distant second in passing situations. Despite Allen's more efficient metrics as a rusher, New York remains committed to Hall as the lead back.

And while the Chargers haven't been great at much this season, they're not particularly friendly to running backs. In the three games since their Week 7 bye, Los Angeles has allowed just 3.6 yards per carry and 76.3 rushing yards per game to the position. And of course, last Monday night, the Chargers held Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to an absurd 14 yards on 13 carries (though Henry salvaged his fantasy day with two touchdowns). Without Henry's value near the goal line, a reliable receiving role or guaranteed volume, Allen is an extremely risky play with a capped ceiling. He's closer to RB2 range than any of the Saints trio, and might crack some starting lineups during the Bye-pocalypse, but I'd work to find an alternative if you can.

What to do ❓ Allen is outside the top 25 but arguably just inside the top 30. You can bench him for sneaky plays like Kyle Monangai or either of the Vikings duo.

WR Jalen Coker, Carolina Panthers vs Baltimore Ravens

Sorry, everybody, but Jalen Coker season is over. Yes, he finished last year hot, and yes, he started this year hot. But since Week 3, it's been basically all downhill. Over the last eight weeks, Coker has averaged just 5.1 fantasy points per game ... 82nd among wide receivers . He's only hit double-digit fantasy points once over that span (12.7 in Week 6) and scored fewer than five points in three of the last four games. Over this particularly concerning past month, he's totaled just seven catches for 74 yards, with a 13.6% target rate (bad) and a 38.9% catch rate (terrible). He still has just one receiving touchdown since his massive season-opener, and is unlikely to find another one with Bryce Young struggling as well.

The matchup with Baltimore isn't particularly scary, but the matchup hardly matters when you're not catching the ball. And the Ravens just proved to be far more susceptible on the ground (against Omarion Hampton and the Chargers), which makes this another great opportunity for Chuba Hubbard to carry the Carolina offense. With Young preferring Tetairoa McMillan, Hubbard and arguably both tight ends (Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble), there's simply too small a piece of too small a pie to trust Coker at all moving forward. He's must-bench material until something changes — and can honestly be dropped in most leagues.

What to do ❓ Coker is well outside of WR2 range and arguably FLEX range as well. You're better off playing lesser names with better production, like Caleb Douglas, Adonai Mitchell and Jakobi Meyers.

WR Emeka Egbuka, Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions

A month or two ago, Egbuka's target share and the matchup with the Lions would have made this an exciting play. But between injury, inefficiency and the complete turnaround for Detroit's defense, it's the exact opposite entering Week 11. Egbuka still hasn't hit 65 receiving yards in a single game all season, and his two decent fantasy outings — in Weeks 5 and 6 — were purely thanks to touchdowns (one rushing and one receiving, respectively). He's averaging an atrocious 1.2 yards per route run and 5.1 yards per target, with a highly unreliable 57.4% catch rate. Even his 23.3% target rate means less than it should, since the Buccaneers are averaging the fewest pass attempts in the league, at just 26.7 per game.

Even coming off the bye, with potential rest for both Egbuka (foot) and Baker Mayfield (foot, thumb), the outlook is particularly poor against this new Lions defense. (Also, Mayfield still might not play, which would force Jalon Daniels back into action.) Since their Week 6 bye, the Lions are allowing just 196.8 passing yards per game in total, with just 5.9 yards per target and a 56.2% catch rate to wide receivers in particular. No wide receiver has topped 12 fantasy points in those four games, with Justin Jefferson's 11.8 setting the high-water mark thanks to the lone touchdown surrendered to a WR by Detroit in that span. Absolutely nothing is playing in Egbuka's favor this week, so he's fully off the fantasy radar as far as I'm concerned.

What to do ❓ Egbuka falls to around the same range as volatile plays like Tre Tucker or Xavier Hutchinson this week ... barring a miraculous touchdown or a huge play, he's going to score somewhere in the low single digits.

TE Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars

Earlier in the year, I really liked Brenton Strange as a streaming candidate, particularly entering the Week 7 bye, when he'd logged 7+ targets and 5+ catches in three straight games. Unfortunately, Strange has only seen seven targets total over the three weeks since the bye, catching six of those targets for 86 yards (with fewer than 25 yards in back-to-back games). He caught a touchdown in Week 10 — his first since the season opener — and that might put him back on the starting radar for managers in a Bye-pocalypse pickle.

But I typically prefer volume to a random touchdown bet with borderline tight ends, and Strange's volume has noticeably dwindled after the bye. It certainly doesn't help that the Jaguars are typically blowing out their opponents and abandoning the pass in the second half — and they're favored by nearly a touchdown against the Giants. I'd understand if you need to stream Strange, given the nature of the position and the week, but I'd recommend looking elsewhere if you can.

What to do ❓ Strange is a fringe TE1, but I'd prefer the ascending Chig Okonkwo, Mike Gesicki in a brilliant matchup, Michael Mayer if Brock Bowers sits or Dallas Goedert.

articles.title: Kansas hosts become guests as Algeria repays World Cup welcome
articles.summary: A bond between Kansas and Algeria has deepened since the city hosted the North Africans during the World Cup.
articles.body:
Algiers, Algeria – Tommee Sherwood never expected that Algeria would come to play such a big role in his life.

Until recently, the 70-year-old from Lawrence, Kansas – a retired university custodian, musician, and volunteer English teacher for refugees – had never been to North Africa before and knew Algeria mostly from the film The Battle of Algiers .

He was aware, though, that Algeria had given refuge to members of the Black Panther Party in the 1970s, including Pete O’Neal, chairman of the Kansas City chapter.

“That connection between Algerians and Kansas City goes way further than most people realise,” he told Al Jazeera.

Sherwood was among 38 residents of Lawrence who visited Algeria from November 9-15 at the government’s expense as a gesture of gratitude from President Abdelmadjid Tebboune for the way their small university city had welcomed the Algerian national team, which used Lawrence as their official base camp during the World Cup.

Five months on, the football was long over, but the genuine bond it had forged between two communities separated by 8,000km (5,000 miles) had only grown stronger.

On a boat in the Bay of Algiers on their first day in the country, a DJ was playing.

“He started playing some old jazz music,” Sherwood recalls in audio messages sent to Al Jazeera. “And he was playing some old timers – some old Kansas City guys that I used to know. It really touched me.”

He gave the DJ a small gift and took photographs. The next day, the same DJ was playing at a different event. He came over to Sherwood and handed him three vintage 45s – old recordings of Algerian singers.

“He told me one of them sang a song to the French. It’s called ‘We Stay, You Go’. I really loved that,” Sherwood said. “These records, if they were made of gold, they wouldn’t be any more valuable to me.”

Sherwood describes the encounters with the DJ as “an example” of the hospitality they were shown by everyone during their time in Algeria.

“I never imagined that the World Cup would open such possibilities for cultural exchange and communication and I’m kind of astounded by it,” Sherwood said.

Five months earlier, Lawrence had hosted Algeria’s national team and its fans with a warmth that touched Algerians. Storefronts on Massachusetts Street flew Algerian flags. The city screened every Algeria and United States match on large outdoor screens. The Kansas University (KU) band played the Algerian national anthem for the team before training.

Algeria was among the 50 countries whose visa applicants faced a $10,000 bond requirement for the tournament, which meant few people from Algeria could make the journey. But the Algerian community in the US, estimated at no more than 50,000 across the country, also came to Lawrence in large numbers.

Saajida Andalsi, an Algerian whose mother has lived in Kansas for more than 36 years, served as an informal bridge between the different communities during the World Cup.

Originally from Algeria, the 24-year-old had not been back for 15 years, but was part of the November delegation. Remembering how Lawrence transformed during the tournament, the 24-year-old said: “My mum kept saying: ‘I didn’t go to Algeria. Algeria came to me’. Lawrence was like a city in Algeria.”

In July, Tebboune ordered the establishment of a twinning agreement between the Algerian town of Tipaza and Kansas City and extended invitations to 100 visitors at the state’s expense.

For Ruth DuWitt, director of community engagement at Explore Lawrence, the city’s tourism bureau, the trip to Algeria deepened her knowledge about the country’s struggle for independence.

Standing in the Casbah of Algiers, she watched the KU band and an Algerian group take the stage together. The Algerian conductor raised his baton over the KU ensemble and directed them through The Star-Spangled Banner, before the KU director conducted Algeria’s national anthem.

“We are standing in that very place – the Casbah – about freedom and revolution and all that spirit,” DuWitt says. “I’m getting choked up just thinking about it.”

“It showed that there wasn’t just connection behind soccer. It was also music. It was the similarities in us just as humans,” she said.

When both bands played together, the crowd was invited into the middle to dance. “It felt like a movie. Nobody could have imagined that happening.”

Madjid Khettar, an Algerian who has lived in Kansas with his family for 13 years, did not make the November trip but has watched the after-effects of the World Cup reshape his daily life.

“Today, when I meet an American and tell him I’m Algerian, he immediately talks to me about the World Cup,” he says. “Even at the football pitch, if one of us is wearing the national team shirt, Americans come up and say they know we’re Algerian and they’re happy to meet us. That didn’t exist before.”

He describes how, when fires broke out in Algeria in August, Americans in Kansas asked how to send aid, and donated when collection links were shared. “That didn’t exist before either.”

Elizabeth Moore Aubin, who was US ambassador to Algeria from December 2021 until January 2026, was part of the Lawrence contingent during the tournament and joined the November delegation to Algiers. She visited more than 50 of Algeria’s 58 provinces or “wilayas” during her posting and built a significant online following.

“As two people groups, Americans and Algerians have more in common than they both realise,” she told Al Jazeera.

She added that it was “great to see subnational diplomacy at work”, but said bonds built through sport need institutional support to last.

“Academic, cultural and sports engagements can all help deepen our ties,” she said. “Those ties then mean more economic and cultural exchange. Everyone benefits.”

Sherwood is already planning to return to Algeria next spring with his wife, primarily to visit refugee camps near Tindouf in the disputed territory of Western Sahara, to help draw US attention to a crisis that is largely ignored in his country.

“It’s saddening that kindness has become such a big news story,” he said of the bond between Lawrencians and Algerians.

“I understand why that is, though, and hope there will be a day when that kindness and mutual respect between peoples is an everyday occurrence. I know we’re a long way from that.”

articles.title: Jets Coach Aaron Glenn Gives Geno Smith Injury Update For Chargers Clash
articles.summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith was set to fully participate in practice Friday and appears on track to start against the Chargers on Sunday.
articles.body: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was scheduled to be a full participant at practice Friday and appears on track to start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday (4:05 p.m. ET on FOX). Smith twice left the Jets’ 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills last Sunday, first to be evaluated for a head injury late in the first half and then after he hurt his left ankle during his only series of the third quarter. He was limited at practice earlier this week, but said Wednesday he intends to play. "He'll be practicing fully today, so we'll see how that goes," coach Aaron Glenn said before practice Friday. "He looks solid. It's very encouraging." The Jets (2-8) are looking to snap a five-game losing streak when they face the Chargers (1-8), who got their first win when they beat the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night. Smith was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik last week. The fourth-round pick from Clemson would make his first NFL start if Smith can’t go, but that doesn't appear to be the case this week. Glenn said the team would see how Smith, left guard Dylan Parham (knee), defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) get through practice Friday before making final calls on their availability for the game at Los Angeles. "We've got two days to see how these guys operate," Glenn said. "It is looking promising for all these guys, so I feel good about that." The offense will be down two wide receivers, though, with Glenn ruling out rookie Omar Cooper Jr. with ankle and hip injuries and Isaiah Williams with a rib injury. Neither was expected to practice Friday after sitting out the other practice sessions this week. Both were hurt against Buffalo. The Jets have Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Tim Patrick and rookie Malik McClain as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Sterling Shepard and Jamaal Pritchett are on the practice squad. Tight ends Mason Taylor and rookie Kenyon Sadiq could also see increased targets in the passing game. "I think that's the good thing about the tight end room is those guys can actually end up playing some of those receiver spots that we have," Glenn said. Williams is the Jets' primary punt returner, so Isaiah Davis could assume that role. Williams also shares kickoff duties with Kene Nwangwu. Defensive lineman David Onyemata, on injured reserve the past eight weeks with an abdominal injury, won't be activated from injured reserve this week, Glenn said. The Jets opened Onyemata's 21-day practice window on Wednesday, so they have two more weeks before they need to either activate him or place him on season-ending IR. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: College Basketball Catchup: A Tournament Record, Oregon's Star, A New-Look Maine
articles.summary: A huge day for NC State's top guard, Katie Fiso leads Oregon to another W, Maine looks completely different, Houston wins a tournament and more from Thursday's college basketball action.
articles.body: An NC State guard dominated in a tournament semifinal. Oregon might have that extra gear it was missing last season. Maine lost its three highest-usage players, but it hasn't mattered one bit. Here's what you need to know from Thursday's slate of college basketball: Top Performance: Paul McNeil Paul McNeil is a 6-foot-6 junior guard for NC State, and on Thursday he had one of the best games of his collegiate career. McNeil scored 33 points with eight assists, five rebounds, two steals, a block and just one turnover and foul each against undefeated Murray State, resulting in a 93-83 victory for the Wolfpack. On top of that, McNeil’s nine 3-pointers are the most by a player in Baha Mar Hoops Thanksgiving tournament play, as well as the second-most he’s ever managed in any game; last December, in McNeil’s career-best effort, he sank 11 3s and scored 47 points. NC State and Seton Hall will now face off in the Baha Mar Hoops championship game — another big showing from McNeil might be just what the Wolfpack needs to down the Pirates, too. 1 Name To Know: Katie Fiso Oregon has been on a roll, winning its fourth game in a row on Thursday. Junior guard Katie Fiso powered the Ducks, scoring 27 points with eight assists, six rebounds and a steal against Fairfield. Oregon would win, 96-75, a strong win against a team that has appeared in three-straight NCAA Tournaments and four of the last five. Fiso was a key contributor for the 2025-26 Ducks as well, but her game has taken a step forward through seven games this season. Fiso is averaging 22.1 points per game, up from 15.5, has added nearly 2.5 rebounds to her average and, despite taking nearly four more attempts per game, has seen her shooting percentage climb to 56%. If Fiso is able to put up a star-level performance — which she’s done so far this year, as she leads Division I in Points Produced, points, field goals, and 2-pointers, and the Big Ten in defensive rebounds — then Oregon could very well have that extra gear it was missing last season. Men's Scoring Leader: Rashad King On Thursday, fifth-year guard and LSU transfer Rashad King had the second 30-point game of his career and his first for Northeastern. King’s 38 points were enough to lead Division I, but not enough for the Huskies, and they would lose to Butler 84-78 despite this. King just didn’t get enough help. Two other starters reached double-digit scoring, with 13 and 10 points, but the bench added just nine points. Butler didn’t shoot as well from the line (66% against 88%), but scored six more points on free throws and sank three additional 3-pointers, too. Women's Scoring Leader: Timea Gardiner Timea Gardiner missed UCLA’s championship season owing to a knee injury, but she’s back with the Bruins now when the roster is in need of veteran support. Gardiner led all D-I women with 29 points on Thursday against Cal Poly, and made a program record nine 3-pointers on 75% shooting to get there. Gardiner didn’t shoot from inside the arc all night but did sink both free throw attempts. On top of the points, she grabbed two rebounds, logged a dime and blocked one shot. Gardiner wasn’t a starter in 2024-2025 and averaged 18.3 minutes per game with 7.6 points and 3.4 rebounds. She’s started each of UCLA’s five games to this point, with career highs in field goal attempts, shooting percentage and 3-point percentage, bringing her to 14.2 points per game. Get To Know A Mid-Major: Maine Maine lost its three leading scorers to graduation, but the roster was going to see even more change than that implied. One of those departed players was forward Adrianna Smith, who led all Division I women in usage rate at 39% last season, was named a Becky Hammon award finalist for the top mid-major player and earned America East Conference Player of the Year honors. She led the conference in scoring (22.8 points), rebounds (10.7) and assists (4.7) — the first men’s or women’s player in America East history to pull that off — and was just the second-ever women’s player in the NCAA to reach 700 points, 300 rebounds and 150 assists in a single season. (The other? UConn legend Maya Moore.) Adrianna Smith: she was pretty good at basketball, and the entire offense revolved around her. With Smith gone — as well as guards Asta Blauenfeldt and Sarah Talon — Maine lost its three top scorers and leaders in minutes. The heavy Smith usage has been replaced with a more team-wide approach, and it’s paying off. After defeating VCU in overtime on Thursday, the Black Bears are now 4-1. Led by junior guard Maddie Fitzpatrick — who redshirted as a freshman and played just nine minutes per game in 2025-2026 — Maine is thriving. Fitzpatrick is averaging 17.4 points per game while leading the America East in rebounds with 10.8, and has five assists per game on top of that. Fitzpatrick didn’t come out of nowhere, either. She attended Cheverus High School in Portland, where she was twice named Maine Gatorade Player of the Year and led Cheverus to two state championships and a regional final appearance. Fitzpatrick averaged 23 points, 11.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 4.9 steals per game her senior season, in which Cheverus not only won the title but was undefeated. She’s joined by returning senior center Lizzy Gruber, who's averaging 11.8 points and 9.2 rebounds so far, as well as senior forward Kaliyah Sain — who scored a game-high 29 against VCU on Thursday — and sophomore guard Lala Woods. She’s managed 15 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game through five contests. Maine’s lone loss so far? A 79-72 defeat against a legit-looking Oregon team. It’ll take time to know if the Black Bears are actually better than they were with one of the best mid-major players in the country, but it’s looking like that’s a possibility. Before You Go: Houston Wins The Players Era 8 No. 8 Houston downed No. 11 Kansas in the Players Era 8 final, 92-83. The Jayhawks made a game of it in the second half by outscoring the Cougars 49-38, but it wasn’t enough to counteract the 20-point gap Kansas had to overcome. The Cougars had one hell of a tournament, defeating Rutgers, No. 1 Florida and Kansas in three games in three days. With No. 2 Michigan State and No. 3 UConn also losing this week, Houston is sure to see a jump in the poll, and already has a couple of seriously impressive wins on its résumé well before Big 12 conference play begins. articles.title: Aina Bauzá se convierte en la primera española en completar la Ruta del Ron
articles.standfirst: Ha cruzado la línea de llegada en Pointe à Pitre (Guadalupe) después de 19 días, 2 horas y 57 minutos navegando en solitario desde Saint Malo
articles.summary: Ha cruzado la línea de llegada en Pointe à Pitre (Guadalupe) después de 19 días, 2 horas y 57 minutos navegando en solitario desde Saint Malo
articles.body: El 1 de noviembre Aina Bauzá puso rumbo a la historia. La mallorquina se convertía en la primera mujer de nuestro país en participar en la Ruta del Ron, un reto colosal que se celebra cada cuatro años y que une Saint-Malo (Francia) con Pointe-à-Pitre (Guadalupe), en el Caribe. En total, 3.542 millas náuticas —6.560 kilómetros— en solitario, sin escalas ni asistencia y con el Atlántico como único escenario. Hoy ha vuelto a hacer historia. Tras 19 días, 2 horas y 57 minutos navegando, se convierte en la primera española en cruzar la línea de meta en Class40, la categoría más numerosa y competitiva de la flota que reúne a 115 embarcaciones, 11 de ellas patroneadas por mujeres. "Estoy muy contenta de haber llegado. La sensación de llegar después de 20 días navegando en solitario es, siempre, increíble. Ha sido una regata muy intensa y con momentos difíciles, pero me lo he pasado muy bien", reconoció Bauzá tras pisar tierra después de más de dos semanas de navegación en solitario. Esta edición de la Ruta del Ron se recordará como una de las más duras de la historia de la regata. Ha estado marcada desde sus primeras jornadas por incidentes en toda la flota. En Class40 se produjeron desarboladas, una lesión que obligó a abandonar a uno de los favoritos, daños de timón y averías que llevaron a varios barcos a retirarse o refugiarse en puerto. En otras categorías hubo vuelcos, daños estructurales y rescates. Tras la salida de Saint Malo, Bauzá tuvo que afrontar viento fuerte, mar difícil, bajas presiones y una ruta más al norte de lo habitual. La travesía incluyó problemas con parte del material, largas jornadas de maniobras y una acumulación progresiva de cansancio. En las últimas jornadas, cuando Guadalupe parecía ya cerca, se enfrentó a todo lo contrario, zonas de viento muy flojo ralentizaron la llegada y obligaron a seguir ajustando cada decisión. La gestión de la autonomía a bordo ha sido otro de los retos de la regata. La producción solar resultó inferior a la esperada, por lo que Aina tuvo que recurrir más de lo previsto al motor para cargar las baterías y controlar con cuidado el consumo de agua y energía. "Tenía muchas ganas de vivir la Ruta del Ron, es una regata mítica y no me ha decepcionado. He aprendido muchísimo y tengo ganas de más, de seguir navegando, aprendiendo y compitiendo", dijo. Un proyecto deportivo y de igualdad Bauzá dio sus primeros pasos en la vela de niña en el Club de Puerto de Andratx (Mallorca). Tras varios años en la vela olímpica y cuando con 26 ya pensaba que la vela de competición se acababa para ella, descubrió otra manera de navegar: la vela oceánica. Desde 2020 ha acumulado más de 40.000 millas de experiencia en Mini 6.50, Figaro y Class40. En 2024 estableció el primer tiempo de referencia certificado por el World Sailing Speed Record Council en solitario entre Cádiz y San Salvador, a bordo del Mini 6.50 REDO. En 2025 fue la primera española en completar la Transat Café L’Or en Class40. La travesía está vinculada a Alice Milliat Foundation, partenaire de impacto y legado del proyecto. La fundación trabaja para mejorar la visibilidad del deporte femenino, reforzar la presencia de las mujeres en todas las profesiones del deporte y promover una práctica deportiva igualitaria y segura.

It sometimes leaves a door open in the opening stages of a fixture as Spain can often require 10–15 minutes to fully wake up. But this fixture against France is a repeat of this past summer’s World Cup semifinal and in that battle, La Roja learned its lesson from the group stage (where it didn’t quite get out of first gear) and started with a bang. articles.title: Lakshya Sen, Satwik-Chirag storm into Hong Kong Open semifinals; Srikanth, Rakshitha bow out
articles.summary: India's Lakshya Sen continued his impressive run at the Hong Kong Open, defeating former world champion Loh Kean Yew of Singapore in three games to enter
articles.body: India's Lakshya Sen continued his impressive run at the Hong Kong Open, defeating former world champion Loh Kean Yew of Singapore in three games to enter the men's singles semifinals on Friday. While Kidambi Srikanth bowed out in the quarterfinals, the men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty also progressed to the last four.The 25-year-old Sen, who has already secured his place in the BWF World Tour Finals, registered a 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 victory over eighth seed Loh in the quarterfinals.The 2022 Commonwealth Games champion, who recently won the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan, will face either Denmark's Anders Antonsen or China's third seed Zhu Xuan Chen for a place in the final.Srikanth exits after straight-game defeatSrikanth's campaign came to an end after he suffered a 17-21, 7-21 defeat against Thailand's world number three Kunlavut Vitidsarn. The Indian had reached the quarterfinals after recovering from a game down to beat Korea's Yoo Tae Bin 12-21, 21-18, 21-14 on Thursday. He had earlier defeated Japan's Koki Watanabe in the opening round.Sen had also beaten Denmark's Rasmus Gemke 21-11, 21-18 in his pre-quarterfinal match on Thursday. Srikanth's first-round victory over Watanabe had helped Sen secure qualification for the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou.Satwik-Chirag enter men's doubles semifinalsIndia's men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty continued their campaign with a 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 victory over China's Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi.The fifth-seeded Indians took 59 minutes to seal the quarterfinal win. After comfortably claiming the opening game, they lost the second before regaining control in the decider.Satwik and Chirag, who have won the Singapore and China Open Super 750 titles this season, will face either Denmark's Daniel Lundgaard and Mads Vestergaard or Malaysia's eighth seeds Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun in the semifinals.Meanwhile, Rakshitha Ramraj's impressive run in women's singles ended in the quarterfinals with a 19-21, 16-21 defeat against Thailand's fifth seed Pornpawee Chochuwong. The 2026 season has been a breakthrough campaign for Rakshitha, who stunned China's second seed Chen Yu Fei 21-18, 24-22 in the pre-quarterfinals on Thursday. articles.title: Elena Congost gana su primera batalla judicial al Comité Paralímpico Internacional
articles.standfirst: El Tribunal de Primera Instancia de París declara "nula e inaplicable" la cláusula de arbitraje invocada por el IPC y su caso será juzgado en la capital francesa con jurisdicción europea
articles.summary: El Tribunal de Primera Instancia de París declara "nula e inaplicable" la cláusula de arbitraje invocada por el IPC y su caso será juzgado en la capital francesa con jurisdicción europea
articles.body: Su caso dio la vuelta al mundo. La maratoniana Elena Congost fue descalificada con polémica en los Juegos Paralímpicos de París 2024 tras ganar el bronce. El Comité Paralímpico Internacional (IPC) le retiró la medalla por soltar durante una fracción de segundo la cuerda que la unía a su guía (Mia Bruguera), con el fin de ayudarle, ya que éste sufría fuertes calambres y corría el riesgo de caerse. En diciembre del año pasado, la atleta española llevó al IPC ante el Tribunal de Primera Instancia de París para solicitar la reparación de los daños, incluida la concesión de la medalla. Sus abogados, liderados por el belga Jean-Louis Dupont, emprendieron acciones legales para que "anulase esta decisión absurda, que vulnera los derechos (libre prestación de servicios) que a Elena y a Mia les confiere el Derecho de la Unión Europea. El Comité Paralímpico Internacional, a través de Paul Fitzgerald, Jefe del atletismo paralímpico, reconoció entonces los "valores de solidaridad y deportividad" mostrados por Congost, pero insistió en que era una violación del reglamento. Según el artículo 7.9, guía y atleta no se pueden soltar en ningún momento. Además, el IPC invocó una "cláusula de arbitraje obligatorio" incluida en el "acuerdo de participación" de los deportistas en los Juegos que todos los paralímpicos se ven obligados a firmar si quieren competir en ellos. Dicha cláusula impone que el arbitraje se celebre en el Reino Unido, es decir, fuera de la Unión Europea, lo que implica que el órgano jurisdiccional estatal competente para un posible recurso de anulación del laudo arbitral será un tribunal británico y no ofrece una vía de recurso ante un órgano jurisdiccional capaz de garantizar el respeto del orden público de la UE (en particular, la libre prestación de servicios) y facultado para plantear cuestiones prejudiciales al TJUE. Este viernes, ha llegado la primera victoria de Elena Congost en el proceso. El Tribunal Judicial de París considera que "la cláusula de arbitraje invocada por el IPC es manifiestamente nula e inaplicable", de conformidad con la sentencia RFC Seraing, y se declara competente para resolver el litigio. Abre, además, un nuevo camino porque cualquier cláusula de arbitraje impuesta por una federación deportiva es manifiestamente nula si la sede del arbitraje se encuentra fuera de la UE. "Me siento satisfecha porque lo que hemos ganado es una cláusula que tiene el Comité Olímpico y Paralímpico y otras Federaciones en la que cualquier queja del deportista te hacen pasar por un Juzgado en Inglaterra con un coste increíble y que se rigen por normas inglesas, no europeas. Es prohibitivo por lo que cuesta. Con esto se consigue que los juzgados europeos tengan competencia para decidir en un caso deportivo. Sabemos que se podrá hacer un juicio en París, donde sucedió todo, con normas europeas", explica Congost a MARCA. Congost y Bruguera están representadas por Dupont-Hissel, Vigo (París), Roca Junyent (Barcelona) y MEO Law (Múnich). Desde Dupont-Hissel han acogido con satisfacción la resolución por la que "todas las cláusulas de arbitraje obligatorio impuestas por las federaciones deportivas internacionales y nacionales (FIFA, UEFA, etc.) deben considerarse «manifiestamente nulas e inaplicables» en el momento en que se refieran a litigios relacionados con cualquier actividad deportiva en el territorio de la UE que tenga una dimensión económica". Además, aboga una vez más por la creación de un TAD UE (Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo de la Unión Europea), que "respete verdaderamente todos los requisitos de un juicio justo, en particular la independencia y la imparcialidad del órgano arbitral, tal y como exigen el artículo 6 del CEDH y el artículo 47 de la Carta de los Derechos Fundamentales de la UE".

articles.title: “I just want them to feel fulfilled”: How David and Victoria Beckham have supported their children’s dreams amid Brooklyn Beckham feud
articles.summary: David Beckham, the Manchester United legend, and his wife, the fashion icon anf popular entrepreneur Victoria Beckham have always known to be an iconic
articles.body: David Beckham, the Manchester United legend, and his wife, the fashion icon anf popular entrepreneur Victoria Beckham have always known to be an iconic couple ever since they started dating in the 90s. While their romance has turned heads for decades, their family feud with their oldest son, Brooklyn Beckham, has dominated headlines for the last few months. Amid this, Victoria Beckham’s comments on how they have raised their four children has resurfaced.Victoria Beckham had shared how she and David Beckham never pressured their children to follow their footstepsA few months ago, in an emotional interview with The Sunday Times Style, Victoria Beckham said, "I think that there's a big difference between supporting children with what they want to do and forcing them…And all we've ever done with any of the children is really support them, encourage them and and help them and individually they've all found what they love, what their passion [is], what their sense of purpose is."The former Spice Girl added, "When the three boys used to play football, one-by-one they decided that that wasn't for them and that's okay…”Victoria Beckham continued, "That's all you can do. I just want them to feel fulfilled. We're very proud of all of them."Over the last few months, as Brooklyn Beckham has continued to make controversial allegations against both his parents and has remained distant from them, neither David Beckham nor Victoria Beckham has spoken about their feud in public.While the rumors of the family feud had been there for the last few years as many speculated that David and Victoria Beckham did not want to associate themselves with their daughter in law, Nicola Peltz, things took a turn for worse when Brooklyn Beckham went public with controversial accusations.In a series of Instagram posts, David and Victoria Beckham’s oldest son, Brooklyn Beckham, accused his parents of wanting to allegedly ruin his wedding and wanting to sabotage his marriage.As per reports, Brooklyn Beckham has also reportedly distanced himself from his siblings but nothing has been confirmed yet.David Beckham and Victoria Beckham continue to show up for their other children amid feud with their oldest sonWhile it has been a long time since David Beckham and the former Spice Girl Victoria Beckham were spotted with Brooklyn Beckham, they have continued to be there for their other children.Recently, the high profile couple were spotted in Paris together as they showed up to be there for their younger son, Romeo Beckham's French tennis movie, Forty Love.For now, all eyes remain on what the family does next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
