articles.title: Netball Horizon Series: England men prepare for historic Jamaica ties with potential World Cup on cards.
articles.summary: England and Jamaica's men's netball teams will act as curtain-raisers for the women's sides in this weekend's Horizon Series in London - and as the sport grows, an inaugural men's World Cup is on the cards.
articles.body:
It's not that men aren't playing it - it's just that you're not seeing it.

That is the message echoed by both James Thomson-Boston - captain of the England men's netball side - and Jamaica defender Authorn Chambers.

These two men's sides have history, and are about to meet again.

In a historic first, their matches will be played as curtain-raisers before England's women, ranked third in the world, face fourth-placed Jamaica in the Vitality Netball Horizon Series in London this weekend.

With an inaugural men's World Cup on the cards, likely within the next few years, BBC Sport looks at the signs that indicate that, if not already, the men's game will soon be on your radar.

Live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website and app

A new era for England Roses under Stembridge - watch on the BBC

The narrative of women's sport fighting for recognition in a historically male-dominated space is a familiar one, but in netball - traditionally a female sport - it is quite the opposite.

Yet in recent years, the rise of the men's game has been meteoric.

The England men's team, known as the Thorns - in contrast to the women's Roses - played their first international in October 2022 and are now coached by women's Netball Super League coach Jo Noel.

They have played international Test series against the likes of Australia, toured St Kitts & Nevis for the Americas Netball Men's Championship, and are now set to play Jamaica for the first time on home soil.

Overseas, Australia and New Zealand contest the Trans-Tasman Cup, while African nations play in the Africa Netball Cup.

And now, 63 years after the first women's World Cup, the sport's global governing body, World Netball, says plans are being developed to host an inaugural men's edition.

In a statement to BBC Sport, it said: "World Netball will always remain proud of the sport's unique female-focused foundations; however we are also a sport that is open to all. We should celebrate and be proud of our traditions but not a hostage to them.

"World Netball feels that now is the right time to intentionally build men into our ecosystem and provide them with an elite platform through which to showcase their skills to the world."

For Chambers, a potential World Cup represents a huge opportunity to get even more eyes on the men's game.

"It needs to be in those kind of spaces that people are seeing it - that's how it's going to grow," he said.

"This sport deserves to have a spotlight on it, be it female or male or altogether," Thomson-Boston added. "I think we just need to keep pushing and keep shouting about it because visibility is key.

"If every men's netball game around the world was now streamed somewhere, you got a notification, you'd realise how many people are actually playing the sport day in, day out."

'Ask every question you want' - changing perceptions

Thomson-Boston moved to England from Australia 10 years ago. While searching for a netball club to join, he was asked if he actually meant a football club.

Now the questions he is asked are often by mothers of young boys, keen to get their sons involved in netball.

"People always apologise in the DMs - 'I'm so sorry to do this', and I'm like, 'no, flood the DMs. Ask every question you want, because you're going to love it when you step out on court'."

Along with that, Thomson-Boston believes the perception of men playing what is, at its roots, a female-led sport, continues to change - even since the captain last spoke to BBC Sport in May 2025.

Instead of people saying "a guy playing men's netball, that seems a bit strange", he says this has now shifted to excitement and curiosity: "How do you train? How do I find out more about it?"

Jamaica's Chambers has been playing men's netball at the elite level for 10 years.

"It's come far since I've been in the sport. In the past, people couldn't openly and comfortably play netball as males," said Chambers, who first played in primary school, subbing in for the girls' team when they were short of players.

"There were stigmas and views on males playing. Now, you're finding more males are being drawn [in]."

The 'two-way' relationship with the women's game

The Roses play Jamaica's Sunshine Girls on both Saturday and Sunday at London's Copper Box Arena, but the Thorns will open the show against the Jamaican Suns before the women take to court.

"We're basically walking with our sisters," said Chambers. "We're playing with our sisters at the Copper Box. It's just an amazing feeling."

There is a closeness between the Jamaican men and the Sunshine Girls, who won silver at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

"We're like their training partners. Our island is small and the best ladies play for the Sunshine Girls," said Chambers.

"They need practice matches. They don't have anybody to play from a female perspective and based on our geographical location.

"We have always supported the Sunshine Girls, and they advocate for us where they can."

In England the picture is similar, but at a club level.

Last year, the England Men's & Mixed Netball Association (EMMNA) launched its first men's Super League.

The England Thorns meet once or twice a month to train in Birmingham, but also train with their respective men's clubs - as well as women's Netball Super League (NSL) sides.

"So many people ask me, 'what happens if the men's game gets bigger? Is it going to start dominating this space that has always been a proudly female-led sport?'" said Thomson-Boston.

The answer to the latter question, he says, is a resounding no. Instead, the aim is solely to grow the sport collectively.

"Because the more eyes on the sport, the more people who enjoy the sport, the more people who play it week in, week out, the more people who start attending Super League - the more sponsors can start to look at the sport as a profitable experience for them."

articles.title: Former NHL forward Daniel Carr under criminal investigation in Switzerland following brutal on-ice attack
articles.summary: Former NHL forward Daniel Carr is facing a criminal investigation in Switzerland following a violent on-ice incident following an attack on an opposing
articles.body: Former NHL forward Daniel Carr is facing a criminal investigation in Switzerland following a violent on-ice incident following an attack on an opposing player. The incident occurred during a brutal incident during a Swiss National League game that left EHC Biel-Bienne captain Gaëtan Haas sidelined with a concussion. The 35-year-old Canadian, who previously played for the Montreal Canadiens, Vegas Golden Knights and Nashville Predators, is currently with HC Ajoie. The incident occurred back on October 16 during a matchup against EHC Biel-Bienne. Reports suggest that, following an investigation, Carr has served a seven-game suspension, while Haas remains sidelined with a concussion.Swiss hockey authorities open criminal proceedings against Daniel Carr after Gaetan Haas incidentFormer NHL forward Daniel Carr is facing a criminal investigation in Switzerland following a violent on-ice attack on EHC Biel-Bienne captain Gaëtan Haas. Following the injury, Haas suffered a concussion and has not returned to the lineup since. According to reports, during a third-period altercation, Carr punched Biel captain Gaëtan Haas in the head while Haas was down on the ice and no longer wearing his helmet. Haas was obviously in a very vulnerable position, but Carr could not have cared less.Following an appeal by Biel, Carr's suspension was increased from five to seven games, accompanied by a fine of 9,040 Swiss francs. He has since served the suspension and returned to action.But, as per recent reports, the situation has now escalated beyond the hockey disciplinary system, and the Regional Public Prosecutor's Office of Berner Jura-Seeland opened criminal proceedings against Carr on October 23, investigating him on suspicion of attempted serious bodily injury.The Bern Cantonal Police have been assigned to investigate the incident and collect relevant evidence. Authorities have also confirmed that both Carr and Haas have already been questioned, with further interviews expected as the investigation progresses.Investigators are reportedly examining television footage of the altercation, along with other available evidence, to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. However, Carr has not been convicted of any offence, and the investigation remains ongoing. The Regional Public Prosecutor's Office of Berner Jura-Seeland will decide on further legal action after the investigation is completed.Carr entered professional hockey as an undrafted free agent after signing with the Montreal Canadiens in 2014. As per the NHL, he appeared in 117 NHL regular-season games, recording 16 goals and 21 assists for 37 points.His most productive NHL campaign came during the 2017-18 season with Montreal, when he registered six goals and 10 assists in 38 appearances.Carr subsequently had brief stints with the Vegas Golden Knights, Nashville Predators and Washington Capitals as well before pursuing his career in Europe.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Balance Renames Research Lab After Shohei Ohtani, Extends Superstar's Contract
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani and New Balance have extended their contract for the rest of his playing career.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani and New Balance have agreed to extend their contract through the remainder of the Los Angeles Dodgers superstar's playing career. The long-term extension announced Friday includes adding Ohtani's name to the brand's Sports Research Lab at the company's headquarters in Boston in a nod to his contributions to athlete research, innovation and product development. The four-time MVP signed with the footwear and apparel company in 2023, the same year Ohtani signed a then-record $700 million, 10-year deal with the Dodgers after spending his first six seasons in MLB with the Los Angeles Angels. "When I first joined New Balance, they saw me as more than just an athlete, and that relationship has only grown stronger over time," Ohtani said in a statement. "There is a lot of trust in our relationship and I’ve always felt like a true partner whether I’m testing products, sharing feedback or helping shape new ideas." The deal has allowed New Balance to expand its presence in Ohtani's native Japan, where musician, composer, singer, actor and video game developer Ryuichi Sakamoto was previously the face of the company as a brand ambassador and featured artist. Ohtani, 32, recently finished second in the National League Most Valuable Player race behind Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong. Last season, Ohtani batted .275 with 30 home runs and 81 RBIs in 135 games. In 14 mound starts, he went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA and 95 strikeouts. He didn’t pitch after July 3 because of knee and biceps injuries that led to his worst offensive numbers since he joined the Dodgers. The Associated Press contributed to this report. articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani tore his Achilles playing soccer, arriving at a Rikers Island press conference in a wheelchair before taking crutches.
articles.body: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has been a busy bee lately. articles.title: Nepali cricket fans in Qatar want to see their team competing with the best
articles.summary: As thousands from Qatar’s Nepali community watch their team play, they hope that the team will rise in global rankings.
articles.body:
Doha, Qatar – On a warm Friday afternoon in Qatar, the country’s only international cricket stadium was a sea of Nepal’s uniquely triangular crimson and deep blue flags.

Nepal’s supporters arrived with flags draped across their shoulders, held them aloft to flutter in the breeze, cheering every delivery and waving them wildly in celebration of every wicket.

The events on the field seemed nearly inconsequential against the loud cheers of the thousands of fans who had filled the West End International Cricket Stadium on the outskirts of the Qatari capital, as the nation with the world’s highest mountain faced the most powerful force in cricket.

Nepal were bowling first against India A – India’s second XI – in their first group match of the Asian Cricket Council’s (ACC) Rising Star Asia Cup 2026 in Qatar.

Indian captain Tilak Varma and his batting partner Kumar Kushagra kept finding boundaries. Nepal’s bowlers faced the wrath and their fielders could barely keep up.

But the noise in the stands barely subsided.

The supporters followed every ball closely, their attention firmly focused on the team they rarely get to watch up close, especially living thousands of kilometres from home.

Qatar is home to at least 367,000 Nepalis, according to the Non-Resident Nepali Association of Qatar, making them the Gulf country’s third-biggest diaspora community.

Pradeep Kumar Yadav was one of the few thousand Nepali fans who were on a mission to provide vociferous support to their cricket team this weekend.

Yadav arrived at the stadium with seven Nepali friends, who had been planning to come as soon as the tournament’s fixtures were announced.

“This is our first time watching Nepal play outside our country,” Yadav told Al Jazeera.

For Nepal’s sizeable diaspora in Qatar, the cricket team provides a reason to gather around a national passion and often draws large crowds.

The supporters are happy to travel to stadiums to back a team that has risen through the international ranks over the past decade.

Nepal’s modern cricketing journey can be traced back to 1996, when the country became a member of the International Cricket Council (ICC) and the men’s team first competed in an international tournament.

The turning point came when the South Asian nation qualified for its first ICC event at the T20 World Cup 2014.

Soon, Nepal’s players were being noticed on the international stage and leg-spinner Sandeep Lamichhane’s selection in major T20 leagues around the world raised the country’s cricketing profile.

Back home, cricket has spread far beyond the capital Kathmandu into towns and villages, backed by efforts to build the sport’s structure at grassroots level.

For Qatar-based fan Himmat Joshi, the Nepali cricket team’s success has resulted in a sharp rise in the popularity of the sport.

“I feel a lot of happiness,” Joshi said while watching the team play against India. “In the past, fewer people followed it but it has grown over the years,” he said.

Mohammad Zahoor, who was among the thousands in the stands, sees the national team’s progress as a source of pride. He describes the Nepalis as a hardworking nation and says the country is building a domestic cricket system capable of competing with higher-ranked international teams.

“There is a lot of pride in seeing Nepali cricketers represent the country. We are a passionate people,” Zahoor said.

The ambitions extend beyond the T20 format.

Nepal’s supporters want to see the country compete against established cricketing nations and eventually earn a place among the teams playing Test cricket.

For Zahoor, defeating a Test-playing country would be an important step towards that ambition.

He also hopes cricket will become part of Nepal’s international identity, alongside its reputation for mountaineering, the Himalayas and being home to Mount Everest.

“Nepalis play the game like a festival,” Zahoor explained.

“Our expectations and hopes are that one day Nepali people are known for their cricket as they are known for their culture of mountaineering and Mount Everest.”

At the stadium in Qatar, the flags, chants and sheer number of supporters reflected that ambition.

In the end, India broke their hearts with a crushing 306-run win.

But it mattered little to the thousands cheering on their team, despite the loss.

For some, including Yadav and his friends, it offered a unique opportunity to watch Nepal play abroad.

Others were simply happy to get a chance to follow a team that has given the country, and its passionate supporters, a growing presence in international cricket.

articles.title: Win Sports presenta contraoferta clave en la Dimayor por la transmisión del fútbol colombiano
articles.standfirst: Giro en los derechos de TV del fútbol colombiano: llega una contraoferta de Win Sports decisiva a la Dimayor a un día de que se decida el nuevo contrato
articles.summary: Giro en los derechos de TV del fútbol colombiano: llega una contraoferta de Win Sports decisiva a la Dimayor a un día de que se decida el nuevo contrato
articles.body: La definición sobre quién transmitirá el Fútbol Profesional Colombiano (FPC) a partir de 2027 ha entrado en su recta final tras conocerse que Win Sports presentó formalmente una contraoferta ante la Dimayor. De acuerdo con el reporte de Blu Radio del 20 de noviembre de 2026, el actual licenciatario activó su derecho de preferencia antes del vencimiento del plazo fijado para este sábado 21 de noviembre, con una propuesta que iguala y supera ligeramente los 90 millones de dólares anuales atribuidos a la oferta externa encabezada por el grupo vinculado a Mauricio Correa. Durante semanas, el futuro televisivo del campeonato colombiano estuvo rodeado de rumores y versiones cruzadas sobre quién disputaría el negocio una vez concluya el contrato vigente el 31 de diciembre de 2026. El punto de partida de esta etapa fue la aparición de una oferta de 90 millones de dólares al año presentada por un consorcio liderado por Mauricio Correa, cifra que elevó drásticamente el listón económico frente a los entre 55 y 60 millones de dólares anuales que, según reportes de prensa, venía pagando Win Sports a la Dimayor. Según ha informado Blu Radio, ante ese escenario, la sociedad integrada por DirecTV y RCN Televisión —propietaria de Win Sports— recurrió a la cláusula contractual de derecho de preferencia, respaldada en su trayectoria y operación de las transmisiones del FPC. Al presentar una contrapropuesta que iguala y supera levemente los US$90 millones antes de que cierre la ventana límite del sábado 21 de noviembre, el mecanismo contractual impide una subasta abierta adicional entre las partes y deja el camino despejado para su continuidad, pendiente de la revisión y ratificación formal de los clubes y directivos de la Dimayor. La recta final de la negociación también ha estado marcada por aclaraciones públicas frente a versiones que circulaban en redes y medios deportivos: Desmentido sobre Caracol Televisión y Ditu: Caracol Televisión salió a desmentir categóricamente que existiera una alianza o acuerdo con Win Sports —ni con la plataforma Ditu— en torno a los derechos del fútbol colombiano. Confidencialidad sobre el oferente y aclaraciones sobre Go Sports: La Dimayor descartó previamente que Go Sports Media S.A.S. fuera la compañía oferente, mientras la identidad exacta del tercero detrás de la propuesta inicial y los detalles definitivos del proceso se han manejado con reserva. Fechas clave en el horizonte: Con el sábado 21 de noviembre de 2026 marcado como el límite para ejercer el derecho de preferencia, la mirada de dirigentes, canales y aficionados apunta a la asamblea de la Dimayor programada para el miércoles 25 de noviembre, instancia en la que se espera el pronunciamiento oficial que defina la adjudicación a partir de 2027. Más allá de quién termine firmando el acta definitiva, el salto económico hacia la franja de los 90 millones de dólares anuales abre dos interrogantes centrales en el entorno del FPC. Por un lado, representa un ingreso superior para la Dimayor y sus clubes afiliados a partir de 2027; por otro, plantea la inquietud entre los seguidores sobre si asumir un costo anual sensiblemente mayor podría traducirse en ajustes en las tarifas de suscripción o en los modelos de acceso para ver los partidos del campeonato

articles.title: Detroit Lions injury update: Cade Mays out, Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield questionable
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions will be without their starting center for a third straight game Sunday, Nov. 22, when they take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions will be without their starting center for a third straight game Sunday, Nov. 22, when they take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers − potentially with Baker Mayfield − at Ford Field.

The Lions ruled Cade Mays out for Sunday's game and listed six other players as questionable.

Safety Kerby Joseph does not have an injury designation and will make his season debut after battling a knee injury since last October.

"Knee's feeling great," said Joseph, who was listed as a full participant in practice on the Lions' estimated practice report.

Cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip), Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) and Khalil Dorsey (ankle), defensive end Tyler Lacy (shoulder), linebacker Joe Bachie (knee) and running back Sione Vaki (ankle) are questionable for the Lions.

Reed said this week he does not expect to play.

Mayfield was a limited participant in practice for the second straight day for the Bucs (3-6) despite battling foot and thumb injuries. Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said this week he expects Mayfield to play.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will start if Mayfield can't go.

articles.title: Bayern held by Cologne as Kane and Olise forced out with injury
articles.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany made his comeback but the Bundesliga leaders were held to a 1-1 draw with Cologne at the Allianz Arena on Friday evening....
articles.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany made his comeback but the Bundesliga leaders were held to a 1-1 draw with Cologne at the Allianz Arena on Friday evening.

They could lose the league lead if Borussia Dortmund beat lowly Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday and Kompany, who had missed the last five games due to illness, will also be concerned about Harry Kane and Michael Olise.

Both stars were forced to abandon the match due to injury. Kane went down in the 20th minute with what appeared to be an ankle injury, while Olise received treatment after making contact with a Cologne defender in the 42nd.

The French forward was initially able to return to the game, but was also subbed off during the break.

Cologne stunned the Bavarians and took the lead in the 12th minute. Mikey Moore received the ball inside the Bayern box and kept his composure to brilliantly round goalkeeper Jonas Urbig before slotting the ball into an empty net.

Bayern, however, were level in the 37th thanks to Nathaniel Brown's low drive from the edge of the box.

Bayern will also be thankful to goalkeeper Urbig for the point after he made a sensational double save in the 59th to deny Said El Mala and Linton Maina.

articles.title: 7 stats to know before the Eagles host the Steelers in Week 11
articles.summary: The Eagles return from their bye to host Pittsburgh at 1 p.m. Here are seven stats to know about the matchup and their home streak
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles return from their bye at 2-7 to face a Pittsburgh Steelers team coming off a 38-18 loss at Cincinnati. The NFL moved Sunday's kickoff at Lincoln Financial Field from 4:25 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Philadelphia has lost seven straight this season but has won 11 consecutive home games against Pittsburgh.

1. Nick Sirianni is unbeaten after the bye

Philadelphia is 5-0 immediately after its regular-season bye under Sirianni. He is the first Eagles coach to win his first five post-bye games since Andy Reid did it from 1999 through 2003. One of Sirianni's five wins came against Pittsburgh in 2022, when Philadelphia won 35-13.

2. Cincinnati exposed Pittsburgh through the air

Joe Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns against Pittsburgh, which trailed 24-3 at halftime. Philadelphia's opportunity starts with giving Joe Milton time to throw. The Giants sacked him seven times in his first Eagles start, including three by linebacker Arvell Reese.

3. Pittsburgh has not won in Philadelphia since 1965

The Eagles began their 11-game home streak against the Steelers in 1966. They extended it with a 27-13 win in 2024, holding Pittsburgh scoreless after halftime and running out the final 10:29. The Eagles are also 5-0 against AFC North teams under Sirianni, according to Philadelphia's Week 11 game notes.

4. Jordan Mailata and Markel Bell face different tests

Mailata has played every Eagles offensive snap and ranks third among tackles with at least 500 snaps with an 88.5 PFF offensive grade, according to the team's game notes. On the right side, rookie Markel Bell faces T.J. Watt. Watch whether Philadelphia sends a tight end to chip Watt before releasing into a route.

5. Makai Lemon has become Milton's most productive target

Lemon leads Philadelphia with 37 catches and 312 receiving yards. He caught six passes for 61 yards in Milton's first start. DeVonta Smith was upgraded to full participation Thursday after missing five of the past six games, while Dontayvion Wicks remained limited. Smith's return would give Milton another option outside while Lemon continues to work underneath.

6. Philadelphia may start two second-year linebackers

Zack Baun and Smael Mondon Jr. were absent Friday, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer's Jeff McLane, who reported that Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. are in line to start inside. That pairing would have to handle Jaylen Warren as a runner and receiver.

7. Aaron Rodgers can test Philadelphia before the snap

Rodgers has 15 touchdown passes this season and 542 in his regular-season career, according to Pittsburgh's game notes. His cadence can force defenders to reveal pressure or coverage early. Nolan Smith has a sack in three straight games, and pressure from four rushers would let Vic Fangio keep safety help available against DK Metcalf.

articles.title: Bayern Munich may try to force Jamal Musiala into a pay cut, admits CEO
articles.summary: FC Bayern are considering the possibility that Musiala may never get back to his best.
articles.body:
In an interview with German newspaper Az, Bayern Munich CEO Jan Chistrian-Dreesen addressed the possibility that Jamal Musiala may have to take a pay cut. The FC Bayern star has been the subject of much debate following his numerous health issues in the last two years, including a chronic neurological problem and the recent recurrence of a tricky muscle injury.

Dreesen was asked whether the club would ask Musiala to adjust his salary.

"If we permanently fail to get back to the level that is compatible with the economic framework, then we will have to sit down and talk to each other," admitted the Bayern CEO (via @iMiaSanMia ). "Nevertheless, we have a contract in place, and that remains valid. That has to be taken into account as well."

While the second line downplays the first, it demonstrates that FC Bayern is beginning to lose patience with Jamal Musiala and his repeated injury issues. It was reported that the club would now increase pressure on the player to get back to his best form. Musiala, for his part, still has the benefit of an ironclad contract with plenty of years left to go. However, with Dreesen making these statements, it shows that Bayern Munich are beginning to consider the possibility that Jamal Musiala may never return to the player he used to be.

articles.title: David Law Slams LIV Invites: ‘Doesn’t Sit Right’
articles.summary: DP World Tour winner David Law questions special invites for LIV golfers, arguing players must earn their spot on the circuit.
articles.body:
David Law isn't buying the idea that special invites fix the European Tour. The 35-year-old Scot says handing out spots to former LIV Golf stars without them earning their way through Q-School feels wrong. He told GolfMagic that the beauty of the game lies in earning every single thing a player gets. This is grumbling and a direct challenge to the new membership rules confirmed for the 2027 season.

Nine former LIV players are set to receive tournament invitations after striking deals with the circuit. Names like Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith, and Bubba Watson are on that list. Joaquin Niemann and Abraham Ancer are also included. The tour says these moves bring huge names back to Europe. Law admits that stars like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton add value by playing full time. But he draws a hard line at the players who skip the usual grind to get in.

Securing playing privileges on the European circuit is a struggle Law understands well. He has felt the pressure of the qualifying school himself. "Giving players a large number of invites when they haven't gone through Q-School to earn their way onto our Tour doesn't quite sit right with me," Law said to GolfMagic. That quote hits the core of the issue. It is about the path they took rather than just hating big names. Bypassing the hard work of Q-School sets a bad example for the kids trying to make it the old-fashioned way.

Some might argue that the tour needs star power to survive. Maybe it does. But the method of getting those stars matters. The DP World Tour confirmed these arrangements just a week before Law spoke up. The list includes legends like Sergio Garcia and Lee Westwood, who returned through the career-money category. That feels different than a free pass. The distinction is clear to Law, even if the tour office sees it differently.

While the LIV debate rages, another rule change is stirring up trouble for the LPGA Tour. Carlota Ciganda knows she is one of the slowest players on the circuit. On Thursday, she posted a 68 to open the CME Group Tour Championship and discussed the new policy. Starting next year, players timed on 35 holes will face a $35,000 fine. That number increases if the problem gets worse. "Obviously, being one of the slowest players, it's not going to help me," Ciganda told reporters. She thinks the fine might not even make that much of a difference in how fast rounds go.

Lindy Duncan, a recent winner on the tour, sees the waste of time in waiting. "When you're just standing there waiting, and the fans are just standing there, waiting, it feels like a waste of time," Duncan said. The LPGA Tour has been strict on this before. While vying for the lead earlier this season, Ciganda was assessed a two-stroke penalty at the Buick Shanghai Invitational. The new financial penalty is a steep jump from the $5,000 fines players saw this year. Ciganda says she will try to play quicker to avoid paying that money. No one wants to hand over $35,000 just for taking their time.

The tour is trying to balance fairness with speed. Law wants players to earn their spots. Ciganda fears the cost of being slow. Both issues show that the rules of the game are shifting under the players' feet.

articles.title: Giancarlo Stanton Causing Yankees Major Lineup Problem
articles.summary: The New York Yankees may have a problem because of Giancarlo Stanton
articles.body:
On Nov. 10, general manager Brian Cashman revealed that Giancarlo Stanton would be back with the New York Yankees in spring training, saying, "He's not going anywhere."

While the Yankees expect Stanton back, his return is actually causing quite a few problems. Stanton cannot play in the field, meaning he is locked into the designated hitter spot. That is causing problems for Luis García Jr. and Aaron Judge.

Last season, Stanton missed most of the year, and García played first base and Ben Rice played designated hitter. With Stanton back, Rice will go back to first base, meaning García will have to go back to playing second base, as he did for his entire career before last season.

It would be really easy for the Yankees to just plug García in at second base if it were not for Anthony Volpe. Volpe looked good after his return from being demoted, and he figures to be part of the equation at second base.

Ultimately, Stanton's return to the team has a ripple effect that essentially takes at-bats away from García. The only way around it is seemingly moving on from Volpe and giving García the keys to second base. Another option would be to move Volpe to third base full-time and move on from Ryan McMahon.

However, as long as McMahon is on the team, the Yankees cannot commit to that plan. However, even if the Yankees were to do that, it's not really an upgrade at third base unless Volpe proves he can actually be a consistent offensive force. Going into the year, having to rely on that is not great.

On top of all of that, the Yankees are reportedly exploring the third base market. If they do add an external third baseman to replace McMahon, then they are really in a bind with García's playing time.

The easiest solution for the Yankees would be to move on from Stanton, play Rice at designated hitter, play García at first base, play Volpe at second base and then add a real upgrade at third base.

Another ramification of Stanton's return is Aaron Judge's health. He missed most of last season, and he is not getting any younger. The Yankees may prefer to get him off his feet to help keep him healthy, but they cannot do that with Stanton clogging the designated hitter spot.

articles.title: Michigan football reveals uniform combination for UCLA, Senior Day
articles.summary: The Wolverines are bringing back a familiar combination for their home finale, one they've worn to three victories this season.
articles.body:
There's one more contest at The Big House this season, and Michigan football has worn all sorts of permutations of its famous uniform.

From the all-maize look in the season opener (resurrected for the first time since its debut against Florida in Dallas in 2017), to the big-game blues worn against Iowa , Indiana, and MSU -- the alternates have been abundant. But, for senior day at Michigan Stadium, the Wolverines will revert to the classic look.

The official Michigan X account posted the uniform combo expected for Saturday against UCLA , and the maize and blue will wear just that -- the winged helmet, with a blue top and maize pants. They'll also wear white accessories.

Michigan has worn the blue, maize, and white combination once this year: in the Week 2 win over Oklahoma . The other times the Wolverines went traditional -- vs. UTEP and Penn State -- the maize and blue wore blue and maize accessories, respectively.

The Wolverines have worn blue tops and maize pants three times this year, and are 3-0 doing so. They are 0-3 wearing 'big game blues,' and 1-0 wearing all maize.

articles.title: Vikings-49ers has massive implications in race for NFC's No. 1 seed
articles.summary: If the Vikings want a bye to the divisional round, Sunday night is essentially a must-win game.
articles.body:
Sunday night's Vikings-49ers showdown in Mexico City has huge seeding implications in the NFC playoff picture. Whoever emerges from Estadio Azteca with a victory will have the inside track to securing the No. 1 seed and the conference's lone bye to the divisional round.

The 49ers come into this game with the best record in the NFC at 8-1. If they win, simulations from Arif Hasan of Wide Left project that they'll have a 68.5 percent chance to secure the 1 seed. They'd have a two-game lead and a tiebreaker over the Vikings, as well as at least a one-game lead over the Lions and Bears.

In that situation, the Vikings would have just a 6.7 percent chance to secure the 1 seed, given that they'd have to make up three games on the 49ers over the final seven weeks. That would potentially require winning out.

However, if the Vikings are able to pull off a minor upset on Sunday night, they'd be in the lead with a 54.3 percent chance to claim the top seed in the NFC. They'd be tied with the 49ers and would hold a head-to-head tiebreaker. If the Lions beat the Buccaneers this week, Detroit would still hold the 1 seed via tiebreaker over the Vikings, but the two teams will meet again in Minneapolis later this season.

A Vikings victory would drop the 49ers' 1-seed odds to 14.8 percent.

articles.title: Hafley Names Kenneth Grant As Next Startership After Phillips Injury
articles.summary: Head coach Jeff Hafley confirms Kenneth Grant will take over defensive snaps after Jordan Phillips' season-ending injury, per Dolphins Talk.
articles.body:
Head coach Jeff Hafley has decided to hand the starting defensive tackle role to Kenneth Grant. This move comes after the team lost Jordan Phillips to a season-ending injury during the week. The decision was made public on Wednesday as the Dolphins prepare for a tough matchup. According to Dolphins Talk , Hafley stated clearly that Grant will immediately be relied upon for a significantly higher number of snaps.

The Dolphins face a massive hole in their defensive line after losing three players in a short time. Zach Sieler is already out for the year, and now Phillips and Zeek Biggers are gone too. Phillips is undergoing surgery and both he and Biggers will go on injured reserve. The team must find a way to stop the run without these key veterans. Hafley praised the toughness of the players who are gone but said the team has no time to dwell on the bad luck.

Hafley did not hesitate when asked about who would fill the void left by Phillips. He pointed directly to the young talent in the locker room who is ready to step up. "It's going to be KG's turn," Hafley said, using the rookie's nickname to show his confidence. Grant has been working hard in practice and the coaching staff wants to see what he can do against a top-tier offense. The coach also noted that Keith Cooper Jr. would see more time after joining from the practice squad. Cooper has shown he can handle the speed of the NFL quickly.

The new players have to learn the scheme fast because they will play on every down. Defensive line coach Austin Clark is calling these extra meetings "night school" to help them study. They need to understand first, second, and third-down calls plus red zone duties. Hafley gave credit to the group for putting in the extra work to get ready. The defense cannot simplify too much or the offense will exploit them for big gains.

Even with the losses up front, the linebacker unit is still performing at a high level. Jordyn Brooks has been a standout player despite the team struggling to win games. Hafley believes Brooks is playing at an elite level that should get him more national attention. "He's playing at an All-Pro level," Hafley said, backing up his claim with the player's consistent play. Brooks has shown he can handle the pressure of a losing season and keep improving his game.

The Dolphins will face the Buffalo Bills on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium. Hafley expects the new defensive linemen to step up and make plays for the defense. The coach also mentioned that Kyle McCord has another week of practice to get better before the big game. "I'd expect him to play better," Hafley said, looking for growth from his young quarterback. The team will see if these changes work when they take the field on Sunday.

articles.title: Bayern Munich 1-1 FC Köln: Initial reactions and Observations
articles.summary: FC Bayern gives away a free point instead of finishing the game off
articles.body:
I'm not kidding you when I say that this game is probably the worst game I've ever watched this season. Forget the injuries to Harry Kane and Michael Olise, the fact that you got outplayed by a team who before this game was hovering above the relegation zone speaks volumes on the team's performance.

The thing that infuriates me the most is the team passing it around the box instead of shooting when there's an opening. There were many opportunities for the players to just shoot but instead they play too nice and set someone up. Köln literally sat back and countered and their remedy for this is mindless passing around the box? It's not going to work all the time.

Jonas Urbig literally rescued a point for Bayern with those successive saves.

That's all for now. Bayern better respond against Lille in the Champions League and away to Hamburg next week. Otherwise, serious questions will be asked of everyone in that club.

87' — Noah Codjo-Evora replaces Aleksandar Pavlović.

58' — Urbig denies Köln with successive saves!

49' — Said El Mala fumbles the free-kick sent in by Linton Maina.

46' — Welcome back! Tim Binder replaces Michael Olise.

Classic post-international break blues, but can it really be confused for Bayern's regular performances so far? The passing is not accurate, the timing and positioning is off, the shooting in general and taking one too many passes instead of just shooting at time. All these factors are off today.

For the credit we give Konrad Laimer, his aggression and propensity to get sucked out of position is a big weakness. This happened against Paris Saint-Germain (second leg) and it happened again today.

Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah were both okay so far, Olise meanwhile is having a subpar game.

Losing Harry Kane to injury is a real kick in the nuts.

articles.title: Charles Leclerc recalls getting stopped by Las Vegas club security as a teenager
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc recalls getting stopped by Las Vegas club security as a teenager and needing his dad to pick him up
articles.body:
Today, Charles Leclerc can headline his own pop-up café at Wynn Las Vegas without waiting in line. Funnily enough, however, back when he first set foot in Nevada, he could not even make it past a nightclub bouncer.

Appearing on The Fast And The Curious podcast during 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix week, the Ferrari driver opened up about why Sin City holds a personal place in his memory - including an awkward underage run-in with security long before Formula 1 arrived on the Strip.

"Las Vegas was the first place I ever went to in the United States with my father back then," Leclerc recalled, referencing a major karting weekend in the city. "I was maybe 15 or 16, and I remember trying to go into a club for the very first time, and I got stopped by security, and my father had to come and pick me up at the security, which [was] quite embarrassing, but it's a funny memory now."

The trip dates back to November 2012 - barely a month after Leclerc's 15th birthday - when he competed in the SKUSA SuperNationals XVI on a temporary circuit at the Rio Hotel & Casino. Even if his nightlife debut ended at the door, his on-track performance stood out: he qualified on pole position in the TaG Senior class and finished fourth in the final.

Leclerc later returned to Las Vegas on vacation with close friends around 2017 or 2018, and laughed when hosts Betty Glover and Christian Hewgill asked if bouncers still gave him trouble.

"I do now, I do, yeah. I'm over 21, so I'm all good now," Leclerc joked. He then paused to ask whether newly crowned 2026 World Champion Kimi Antonelli had turned 21 yet, only to realise the 20-year-old Mercedes driver is still barred from Vegas clubs himself.

From karting memories to cold-weather challenges

Since Formula 1 added the Las Vegas Strip Circuit to the calendar in 2023, the venue has been kind to Leclerc. He took pole position and finished runner-up to Max Verstappen in the inaugural race, followed by back-to-back fourth-place finishes in 2024 and 2025.

"I love city tracks, and by definition I also really enjoy Las Vegas, but it's a particular track because it has such low grip and also the temperatures are so low that it has its own challenges," Leclerc said.

On the podcast, he warned that cold conditions remain one of Ferrari's biggest weaknesses in 2026. Even so, Leclerc made an encouraging start in Thursday night's rain-hit second practice, clocking third fastest behind Mercedes' George Russell and Alpine's Pierre Gasly as Ferrari tries to keep its late-season momentum alive.

articles.title: Blues’ Three Surprises Prove This Season Is No Fluke
articles.summary: Joel Hofer's elite stats, Justin Barron's waiver claim, and Adam Jiricek's debut show the Blues have real depth beyond the disappointment.
articles.body:
The St. Louis Blues started the 2026-27 season with a 10-9-2 record, a mark that suggests a team stuck in the middle of the pack. These are lucky breaks and genuine shifts in the team's identity that could carry them through a long winter.

Joel Hofer has taken the starting net and refused to let go. He is playing well and among the best in the entire league at stopping goals that should have gone in. MoneyPuck states that Hofer's 8.2 Goals Saved Above expected ranks third in the NHL among goalies who have played 15 or more games. That number is wild for a team that often struggles to score. He has become the backbone of the franchise, and if his teammates can finally feed him the puck, he might get serious talk about the Vezina Trophy.

Justin Barron arrived in St. Louis after being cut by the Nashville Predators. In just 19 games, he has scored four goals and added nine assists for 13 points. He also owns a stellar 55.36 expected Goals-For percentage, which shows he drives play better than almost anyone else on the blue line. A full season of this performance could give Barron a claim to being the greatest waiver claim in franchise history. As noted by Bleedin' Blue , it would be wonderful for the Blues to possess their own version of "the Florida Panthers claimed Gustav Forsling" story. The team found a top-four defender for pennies on the dollar.

Adam Jiricek was not on the opening night roster, but injuries forced a quick call-up that turned into a success story. He played 17 games and looked like a player ready to stay, even if his point total was low with just one goal and two assists. His on-ice impact was promising for a 20-year-old defenseman, and his 51.58 expected Goals-For percentage at 5-on-5 was a solid mark. He has earned another look should the Blues need someone to fill the backend again. The team now has depth that was missing just a month ago.

The Blues are 10-9-2 through 21 games, and three players are contributing in unexpected ways.

articles.title: Why wild 49ers anomaly ought to put fright into Vikings fans
articles.summary: The 49ers have seemingly been hit with injuries more than any other NFL team in recent years. So it’s notable any time they have a relatively clean bill of h...
articles.body:
The 49ers have seemingly been hit with injuries more than any other NFL team in recent years.

So it's notable any time they have a relatively clean bill of health.

That was the case on Friday as Kyle Shanahan's team had something extremely rare happen: All 53 players on the active roster participated in practice ahead of their key game against the Vikings, with the winner earning the No. 1 seed in the NFC through the first 11 weeks.

That includes star receiver Mike Evans , who is officially listed as questionable for Sunday night's key game in Mexico City after missing the last three contests with Achilles tendinitis.

Having all active players at practice doesn't mean the 49ers are completely healthy, but it's a step in the right direction. They didn't rule any players out for the Vikings game on Friday.

The team is still listing Evans, linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck), defensive tackle C.J. West (knee), cornerback Nate Hobbs (adductor), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder, neck), pass rusher Khalil Kareem (ankle), backup quarterback Mac Jones (illness) and linebacker Luke Gifford (chest) as questionable.

There remains some uncertainty regarding West and Hobbs, who remain on injured reserve. They could be activated before the game. The 21-day practice window for Hobbs closes on Wednesday, while West has until Dec. 2.

Additionally, the 49ers have three of their eight return designations from injured reserve available. Candidates for those include rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, second-year linebacker Nick Martin, running back Isaac Guerendo and pass rusher Sam Okuayinonu.

articles.title: The most important stat was actually injuries in Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw with FC Köln
articles.summary: FC Bayern will want this game back in a big way.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich's 1–1 draw with 1. FC Köln was a pretty remarkable statistical contradiction.

Vincent Kompany's side controlled practically every aspect of possession, but the numbers suggest that control did not translate into meaningful attacking superiority.

Bayern finished with 71% possession, completed 732 passes at a 92% accuracy rate, registered 17 shots, and won five corners without allowing Köln a single one. Bayern also recorded 35 touches in the opposition penalty area compared to Köln's 22. By most conventional measures, Bayern dictated the match.

However, the more important numbers tell a different story. Despite taking 10 more shots than Köln, Bayern managed just one effort on target. Bayern's expected goals total was only 0.94, less than half of Köln's 1.98. The visitors also generated five big chances compared to Bayern's two.

Even more frustratingly, Bayern missed two of its big chances, while Köln squandered four. Both teams had opportunities to take all three points, but neither could capitalize enough to secure the victory.

Ultimately, Bayern's problem was not a lack of possession or attacking activity. It was an inability to turn territorial dominance into genuinely dangerous opportunities while allowing Köln to create considerably better chances with far less of the ball.

When you factor in this stat, it tells a little more of the tale for the game:

Injuries to Harry Kane and Michael Olise: 2

A 1–1 draw was the result, but the underlying numbers suggest Bayern Munich should have been much better.

articles.title: Archie Griffin on Ohio State's season, Ryan Day, favorite OSU memory
articles.summary: What sat down with Ohio State legend, Archie Griffin to talk Buckeye football, Ryan Day, and his favorite OSU memory. It was fun and insightful.
articles.body:
There is only one two-time Heisman Trophy winner in the history of college football, and his name is Archie Griffin. He's also one of the great ambassadors Ohio State has ever had — still around the program, still invested, still the guy everybody wants to hear from when things get tough.

And things have been tough, at least when it comes to standards set on the banks of the Olentangy. When we caught up with Griffin last week, the Buckeyes were sitting at 6-3 after a rough stretch, with three games left on the schedule and a fan base that was frustrated. Ryan Day was catching heat, and the defense was giving up points in bunches. OSU has since gotten back in the win column with a victory over Northwestern , but it's still a season folks aren't used to in Columbus.

We wanted to know what Archie thought — about where this team is, about the man leading it, and about the moment that still stands out most from his own playing days in the Scarlet and Gray. What follows is the transcript of three questions Griffin was nice enough to answer, and we thought they were insightful, and maybe you will to.

On where Ohio State stands in the midst of a somewhat difficult season

(Harrison) - So, difficult season for Ohio State. I know you're in the program; you've been around the program. Give us your take on where this team is. I mean, listen, a lot of programs would love to be six and three, right? But it just doesn't cut it at Ohio State. And so Ryan Day's come under a lot of fire, the fans are upset, all of that. Can you give us your take on what you believe has happened this season with Ohio State? What's contributed? Obviously, Julian Sayin going down didn't help. But what's your take on where this team is, and what has contributed to the three losses that Ohio State has seen so far?

(Griffin) - "Well, first of all, we probably had one of the most difficult schedules in the country. So it was not going to be a walk in the park anyway. But we knew we had a difficult schedule, and we're going out and trying to play this tough schedule right now. We're sitting at three losses and have three games to go, which could be tough games, because you've got that team up north on the schedule at the end of the season. But Northwestern is playing great football, who we play this week. And Nebraska is playing outstanding football. So, I mean, we've got tough games ahead of us.

"So from my standpoint, we can't look back. Those games we played, they're in the past, and we lost those football games. We've got to move forward. We've got to take care of business ahead of us. And you mentioned some of the reasons that we've lost some of those games. Certainly, Julian Sayin was a huge part of that. I mean, he was a Heisman Trophy finalist last year, and if you lose a Heisman Trophy finalist like Julian Sayin, you're going to suffer a little bit. And we have suffered a little bit.

"But the thing that I think we've got to really, really get together is the defense. I'm not used to Ohio State teams giving up 40 points in a game. Or 30, or even 30 points in a game. And so to me, we'll get that part squared away and keep working on our offense with our new quarterback. I think we'll be fine the rest of the way, but it's not going to be easy. It's going to be tough, but we've got to remember tough times make tough people.

"You can't ponder what's happened in the past. You've got to move forward. The biggest thing about athletics, especially about the game of football — the best lesson that I've ever learned is that when you get knocked down, you get back up.

"And our young men have to get back up right now. They can't look back at the past, other than to study it to see what happened. But they can't look back at the past. They've got to move forward and take care of business ahead of them."

On the direction of Ohio State under head coach Ryan Day

(Harrison) - Great. Okay. Tell us culture-wise. You're part of the program. It's a good culture at Ohio State. I've kind of been, I guess, a Ryan Day apologist. I think he's a great person. I think he's a great man. I think he gets the big picture. He's coming under fire right now. Can you just give us an idea of what you know about Ryan Day, the person?

(Griffin) - "Well, I know that Ryan Day will do fine. In this situation, he doesn't like being under fire. Who does? Nobody. But I think he's going to get better because of it. He's going to find the solution to the problems that we're having. I have a lot of faith in him. People have got to remember, this is the same man that won a national championship a couple of years ago. He will be back. We will recover from this, and we will make Buckeye Nation proud of the Buckeyes."

On Griffin's favorite memory as an Ohio State player under Woody Hayes

(Harrison) - We've just got a couple more minutes here, so a couple more quick questions for you, if you don't mind. What's your favorite memory as an Ohio State football player?

"My favorite memory was my freshman year at Ohio State. My freshman year was the very first year that freshmen were allowed to play varsity football. And with that being the case, my number one goal was to make the varsity team. Well, when I reported to camp, I was put at tailback on the fifth string of the scout squad. And I didn't really think that I would move up to the varsity, but my goal was to make the varsity.

"Well, the first game of that season was a Big Ten game. It was against Iowa. And the night before the game, Coach would take the players away to the hotel — the varsity players — and we, as freshmen and reserves, we stayed in the dormitories. We met up with the varsity team at the stadium.

"Well, that game against Iowa started, and we were beating them by a pretty good score in the fourth quarter with a couple of minutes to go, and we gave a few freshmen a chance to play. And I was one of the freshmen. And I can remember getting in the game and looking at this as my big opportunity. First play called was an 18 sweep, pitch out to me around the right side. I was excited about this opportunity. I got the pitch and I fumbled. And I thought that was it, that I would never get a chance again.

"And the next game that we had — we had a bye the next week, but we had a game two weeks later after that game. It was also a home game, and because it was a home game, Coach Hayes allowed everybody to dress again. The night before the game, he took the varsity away to the hotel, the rest of us reserves stayed in the dormitories, and we met up with the varsity team at the stadium. The game against North Carolina started.

"And I was still practicing on the fifth string of the scout squad, but the game against North Carolina started. And in the first quarter, North Carolina blocked a punt of ours and went ahead of us seven to nothing. And all of a sudden, a call came from the bench: "Griffin!" They kept calling "Griffin!" And I knew he wouldn't be talking to me — I'm the fifth-string tailback. I hadn't played the week before. He couldn't mean me. But he kept calling "Griffin!" And I was the only Griffin on the team at the time, so I went up to Coach Hayes. He grabbed me by the shoulder pad and told me to go in at tailback.

"I went into the game, and I was in a daze the whole time. But all I can tell you is my number kept being called, and I was running with the ball. And when I came out of the game, I think it was the fourth quarter, the 86,000 fans stood up and gave me a standing ovation, and they did that because in those two and a half quarters, I had rushed for 239 yards.

"And to me, that was the most exciting moment, not only that I ever had at Ohio State, but that I ever had playing the game of football, because to me, that was a miracle. I had no idea that I would get in the game, and I always prayed to have an opportunity to play. And I prayed that night before that game, and he gave me that opportunity. So I'm so very, very thankful for it."

We want to sincerely thank Archie for taking the time to sit down with us and talk about Ohio State football. We also want everyone to know about an article we wrote earlier about the Abbott and Big Ten's "We Give Blood" competition . There's still time to give to such a worthy cause and log it towards Ohio State so Buckeye Nation can come in first place.

Remember, as Archie would say from his time playing for Woody Hayes, "pay it forward" whenever you have a chance.

Contact/Follow us @BuckeyesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Ohio State news, notes, and opinion. Follow Phil Harrison on X.

articles.title: Lely high school taps familiar face to lead Trojans football program
articles.summary: Lely hired alum and former assistant coach Stavros Giarimoustas to lead the Trojans football program, the school announced Friday, Nov. 20, 2026.
articles.body:
Lely at Barron Collier FHSAA high school football game photo gallery

As it was getting ready to start Thanksgiving Break, Lely High School announced it hired former assistant coach Stavros Giarimoustas to lead the Trojans football program.

Lely principal Jennifer Bledsoe met with the team to share the news on Friday, Nov. 20. Giarimoustas replaces interim co-head coaches Carlos Cornelio and Kit Fowler. Cornelio and Fowler took over for first-year head coach Dan Nieboer , who was fired in September following an 0-3 start that saw the Trojans outscored 166-0. Lely finished the season winless at 0-10.

Giarimoustas, known as "Coach G," is a 2005 Lely graduate who played under former Trojans coach Steve Metzger and was later an assistant for him. He's worked at Lely the last three years as an ESE assistant in the classroom and was an assistant football coach for Barron Collier this fall.

"His deep connection to our campus, traditions, and community gives him a unique perspective on the values and expectations that define Lely Football," Bledsoe wrote in a release.

Giarimoustas has over 20 years of coaching experience in Collier County, specializing on defense where he's coached linemen, linebackers and has been a defensive coordinator at four schools, including Lely.

"His extensive coaching experience, combined with his passion for Lely and deep roots within our community, make him an excellent fit to lead our football program," Bledsoe wrote. "Coach Giarimoustas understands the importance of building character, fostering academic success, and developing a culture of excellence on and off the field."

"I cannot wait to seize this amazing opportunity," Giarimoustas said in the release. "I will do everything in my power to give our current Trojans the habits and mindset to carry with them for a lifetime, just like my coaches did for me."

53rd annual Coconut Bowl football game photos between Naples and Lely

Lely put together an impressive 2025 campaign, going 8-4 with a regional semifinal appearance before falling to Miami Central. The Trojans opted to move on from head coach Ben Hammer after three seasons . He led the program to a 20-14 record with a pair of playoff appearances with an offense that averaged 471.2 yards and 45 points per game in his final season.

Nieboer was hired away from Jason Witten's Liberty Christian (Texas) squad in March to replace Hammer leading the Lely football program.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Stifled By Texans Defense In Thursday Loss
articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor rushed for just 21 yards as the Colts fell to the Texans. See the stats, the game script, and what it means for fantasy owners.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor managed only 21 rushing yards on 11 carries during Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans, according to RotoBaller NFL . The former Wisconsin Badger added six receiving yards on four catches while playing in a game where his team fell behind early and tried to catch up. According to RotoBaller, Taylor did not score double-digit PPR points in three of his four most recent games.

The defensive front in Houston made it hard for Indianapolis to move the ball. Taylor gained just 14 yards on his first four attempts and did not find much room after that. His team entered catch-up mode in the second half, which changed how the offense ran the ball. Quarterback Daniel Jones was benched for backup Anthony Richardson Sr. as the game slipped away.

When a team is down by a large score, running the ball becomes less useful. The Colts needed to pass the ball to score quickly, but the quarterback could not connect on long throws. RotoBaller noted that Taylor's stability in the passing game is a plus, but it is also a double-edged sword because it stems from the quarterback's inability to attack deep.

Jones struggled to get anything going downfield, which kept the offense in short-yardage situations. This dynamic forced Taylor to be a primary target for short passes even when the run game was dead. The result was a player who was essentially phased out of the game plan as the second half wore on. The offense needed a spark, but the game script dictated a pace that did not favor the running back.

Week 11 marked a rough stretch for the star back. This trend makes him much more dependent on the game script, especially for a rebuilding Colts squad. When the team is winning, he can carry the load. When the team is losing, his value drops fast because the offense shifts to passing.

The Houston Texans defense did exactly what the Colts needed them to do. They stopped the run early and forced Indianapolis to abandon their ground game. Taylor's 21 yards on 11 carries show a clear lack of room to run. He had four receptions on five targets, which shows he was still involved, but the yardage was minimal. The defense did not allow the Colts to control the clock or the pace of the game.

David Montgomery, the Texans running back, returned from injury to help the offense. He completed a full practice session for three consecutive days leading up to the matchup. This return gave Houston a balanced attack that Indianapolis could not match. While Montgomery got his snaps, Taylor saw his opportunities shrink as the game progressed. The Texans controlled the line of scrimmage and kept the Colts off balance.

The matchup against the Colts' secondary was a key factor for the Texans. Tank Dell, who returned from a knee injury, continued his comeback story. He had three catches for 21 yards in the previous week but stayed involved enough to be a reliable option. The Texans offense moved the ball better than the Colts, which kept their defense fresh and ready to stop the run.

Taylor is a high-end talent, but his production is now tied to the game script. RotoBaller noted that Taylor aims to regain fantasy form during the upcoming home game against the New York Giants. The Giants defense may be more manageable than the Texans front, but the risk remains high.

Anthony Richardson Sr. is now the quarterback for the Colts. It is unclear if this change will help or hurt the offense. Richardson has a different skill set than Jones, which could open up the run game or make it worse. The coaching staff has not said if Richardson will start the next game.

articles.title: Giants Rookie Malachi Fields Proves He Is Ready For More Touches
articles.summary: Giants rookie Malachi Fields has zero drops and 350 yards. Coaches and teammates say he is ready for a bigger role this Sunday against Jacksonville.
articles.body:
Malachi Fields is not acting like a rookie. Through nine games, the Giants third-round pick has recorded 350 yards and one touchdown by catching 22 of 38 targets. He has yet to drop a pass. This reliability stands out in an offense that often struggles to move the chains. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy says he is not surprised by the rookie's steady play. The team traded up to get Fields in April, giving up picks in 2026 and 2027 to secure his spot at number 74 overall.

Fields has become a key part of the passing attack behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely. He has 10 receptions for 185 yards over his last three games. His big gain came in the recent loss to Washington where he had three catches for 62 yards. The offense looks different now that J.J. McCarthy took over as the starter in Week 7. McCarthy has given Fields more chances to make plays in space.

Matt Nagy believes Fields has a long way to grow. "Not surprised at all with him," said offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, according to Sports Illustrated . "You all have heard me talk about him all camp. His ceiling — when we have this conversation five years from now, you're going to think about this question you're asking me because he's really good." Nagy told reporters on Thursday that the rookie does everything right. He catches the ball, blocks for runners, and makes plays when needed. The coordinator thinks the rookie's potential will keep getting higher.

Nabers agrees with the high praise. He highlighted Fields' ability to separate from defenders and track the ball in the air. "Yeah, I mean, just giving him the ball in space, I think he gets open pretty well. I think he has good feet for how tall he is, he runs fast, can track the ball well. He gets in and out of his breaks," Nabers said, according to Sports Illustrated . The veteran receiver is happy to see the team give Fields more opportunities to find his rhythm.

Isaiah Likely no longer views Fields as a typical first-year player. The tight end sees a teammate who understands how defenses work. "I don't really look at Malachi as a rookie anymore. I look at him coming into his own," Likely said, according to Giants Wire . He explained that when defenses focus on him and Nabers, Fields must win his one-on-one matchups. Likely feels the rookie has done a great job of winning whenever he is asked to.

Fields knows his role in these situations. He understands that if he gets single coverage, the ball is likely coming his way. "But Malachi's definitely honed in on knowing that if I get one-on-one coverage, ball is most likely going to me. So I've just got to make my play," Likely said while describing the rookie's mindset. This awareness helps the Giants offense keep moving even when the other team loads up against the top targets.

The Giants will test this growing chemistry on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 p.m. ET against the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife Stadium.
